```
\subsection*{Motivation}

Let $H$ be a universal inductor, in the sense of a \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.03543}{logical inductor} conditioned on bitstrings that represent the proven theorems of a deductive process.\footnote{Here we're primarily using
\href{https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/FnH2G832sWMySptp5}{this explanation of universal inductors} by ``Diffractor'' as a guide for the setup.} $H$ should be thought of as a bounded reasoner that, in some way, represents evolving human opinions over time. Then, suppose another universal inductor $A$ is constructed as a strictly more computationally powerful reasoner that is trying to predict the future states of the human reasoner. Suppose then that we augment the deductive process of $H$ further by giving it access to outputs of $A$, in an attempt to leverage $A$'s additional computational power to arrive faster at humanity's own trusted future beliefs. The following construction makes that concrete. [Summary of findings after finishing]


\subsection*{Construction}

\paragraph{Base reasoner.}
Take a propositional language $\mathcal{L}$ with sentence set $\mathcal{S}$, a
theory $\Gamma$, and a $\Gamma$-complete computable deductive process
$D_H=(D_H^t)_{t\ge1}$. Let $\mathcal{C}_H$ be a complexity class closed under
polynomial overhead \footnote{explanation of polynomial overhead} and let $H=(H_1,H_2,\ldots)$ be a \emph{universal inductor}
over $D_H$ against $\mathcal{C}_H$: a market each of whose stages $H_t$ is a probability measure over the worlds of $\mathcal{L}$, concentrated on
the worlds propositionally consistent with $D_H^t$, satisfying the logical induction
criterion against traders in $\mathcal{C}_H$. Existence of such a
measure-valued inductor over an arbitrary computable deductive process is
Lemma~\ref{lem:existence}.

\paragraph{Propositions and deferral.}
Choose a strictly increasing, $\mathcal{C}_H$-computable ``deferral" function
$F:\mathbb{N}^+\to\mathbb{N}^+$ with $F(n)>n+1$. Fix an effective enumeration
$P^{(0)},P^{(1)},\ldots$ of $\mathcal{S}$. Since the enumeration is arbitrary, take
$P^{(n)}$ to be some $n$-th proposition of interest, so that tying contract $n$
to statement $P^{(n)}$ costs no generality.

\paragraph{Threshold symbols.}
For each $n\ge1$ and $1\le k\le n$ introduce two fresh propositional symbols:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $\alpha_{n,k}$ representing ``the contract for $P^{(n)}$ deferred to $F(n)$ has value at least $k/n$";
  \item $\beta_{n,k}$ representing ``$A$'s published quote for that contract is at least $k/n$."
\end{itemize}
Let $\mathcal{L}^\alpha:=\mathcal{L}\cup\{\alpha_{n,k}\}$ and
$\mathcal{L}^\beta:=\mathcal{L}\cup\{\beta_{n,k}\}$, with sentence sets
$\mathcal{S}^\alpha$ and $\mathcal{S}^\beta$ respectively, each extending $\mathcal{S}$. The $\alpha$ symbols allow $A$ to price
the future credences of $H^+$ while the $\beta$ symbols
allow $H^+$ to record $A$'s outputs. Because each of these sets of symbols represents threshold sentences, that is claims that a value is at least $\frac{k}{n}$, they respect the monotonicity axioms:
\[
\{\alpha_{n,k}\to\alpha_{n,k-1}\}\quad\text{and}\quad
\{\beta_{n,k}\to\beta_{n,k-1}\}\qquad(n\ge1,\ 2\le k\le n).
\]
For a world $W$ consistent with these axioms each truth-set is an initial
segment, so we can define values as proportions of true threshold sentences:
\[
\mathrm{val}^\alpha_W(n):=\tfrac1n\#\{k:W(\alpha_{n,k})=1\},
\qquad
\mathrm{val}^\beta_W(n):=\tfrac1n\#\{k:W(\beta_{n,k})=1\}
\]
each taking the form $m/n$ for an integer $0\le m\le n$. Using these values, the addition of the threshold symbols to the language allows for the representation of a real-valued unknown rounded to the nearest $\frac{1}{n}$.

\paragraph{Contracts and quotes.}
Define the deferred contract $C_n$ and the quote ledger readout $R_n$ as affine combinations
\[
C_n:=\tfrac1n\sum_{k=1}^n\alpha_{n,k},
\qquad
R_n:=\tfrac1n\sum_{k=1}^n\beta_{n,k},
\]
so $W(C_n)=\mathrm{val}^\alpha_W(n)$ and $W(R_n)=\mathrm{val}^\beta_W(n)$
for consistent worlds $W$. Note that both $C_n$ and $R_n$ are affine combinations of symbols
already in the markets used for convenience rather than separately traded objects. Write
\[
a_n:=A_n(C_n)=\tfrac1n\sum_k A_n(\alpha_{n,k})\in\mathbb{Q}\cap[0,1]
\]
for $A$'s published quote on the deferred contract and
\[
Y_n:=H^+_{F(n)}(P^{(n)})
\]
for the eventual credence of $H^+$ that the contract uses for settlement. 

\paragraph{The more powerful reasoner.}
Let $\mathcal{C}_A\supseteq\mathcal{C}_H$ be a complexity class closed under
polynomial overhead for which the map $n\mapsto Y_n$ is $\mathcal{C}_A$-computable
in the coupled system. More precisely, given $n$, an implementation in $\mathcal{C}_A$ can simulate the mutual construction up to stage $F(n)$ and output $Y_n$. Writing $R(t)$ for the per-stage runtime of the
implementation of $H^+$, we assume $\mathcal{C}_A$ contains $n\mapsto R(F(n))$ (e.g.\ $\mathcal{C}_H=\mathrm{P}$, $\mathcal{C}_A=\mathrm{EXP}$, $F(n)=2^n$ when
$R$ is polynomial). This is a significant idealizing assumption about the computational power of $A$, but note that the fact that simulation is in the complexity class of $A$ doesn't entail that there is any efficient algorithm for traders to implement. Let $\sigma:\mathbb{N}^+\to\mathbb{N}^+$ be
$\mathcal{C}_A$-computable with $\sigma(n)>F(n)$ and such that $Y_n$ can be computed by this simulation
within $\sigma(n)$ steps.

\paragraph{The inductor $A$.}
We will now define $A$ and $H^+$ as two inductors that can see each other, constructed via recursion. For $0\le m\le n$ write the settling profile
\[
\mathcal{A}_n(m):=\{\alpha_{n,k}:k\le m\}\cup\{\neg\alpha_{n,k}:k>m\}
\]
and let
\[
m_n^*:=\argmin_{0\le m\le n}\left|\tfrac mn-Y_n\right|
\]
with ties going to the lower $m$. We therefore have
\[
\left|\tfrac{m_n^*}{n}-Y_n\right|\le\tfrac1{2n}
\]
because the grid $\{0,\frac1n,\frac2n,\ldots,1\}$ has mesh size $\frac1n$, so every value in $[0,1]$ is within $\frac1{2n}$ of some grid point. Define the computable deductive process
$D_A$ over $\mathcal{L}^\alpha$ as one that, for each time step $t$, $D_A^t$ includes:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
  \item the $\alpha$-monotonicity axioms for $n\le t$;
  \item for each $n$ with $\sigma(n)\le t$, the profile $\mathcal{A}_n(m_n^*)$.
\end{enumerate}
Each $D_A^t$ is finite (axiom schemata and settlement profiles are finite at any finite stage) and consistent (distinct $n$ touch disjoint symbols for both axioms and profiles, settlements are initial segments respecting monotonicity). $D_A$ is
computable as part of the mutual construction, since $\sigma(n)>F(n)$ makes $Y_n$ available from $H^+$
before its settlement is required by $D_A$. Let $A=(A_1,A_2,\ldots)$ be a universal
inductor over $D_A$ against $\mathcal{C}_A$.

\paragraph{The inductor $H^+$.}
Symmetrically write
\[
\mathcal{B}_n(\ell):=\{\beta_{n,k}:k\le\ell\}\cup\{\neg\beta_{n,k}:k>\ell\}
\]
and let
\[
\ell_n^*:=\argmin_{0\le\ell\le n}\left|\tfrac\ell n-a_n\right|
\]
with ties going to the lower $\ell$. This is the rounding of $A$'s posted quote. Define the computable deductive process $D_H^+$
over $\mathcal{L}^\beta$ as one that, for each time step $t$, $D_H^{+,t}$ includes:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
  \item $D_H^t$, so that $D_H^+$ extends the base human deductive process;
  \item the $\beta$-monotonicity axioms for $n\le t$;
  \item the profiles $\mathcal{B}_i(\ell_i^*)$ for each $i$ with $i < t$, i.e., the one-step-delayed record of $A$'s published quotes up to the prior time step.
\end{enumerate}
In other words, $D^+_H$ augments $D_H$ with feedback about the quotes produced by $A$. Each $D_H^{+,t}$ is finite and
consistent just as $D_A$ is, and it is computable as part of the
recursion since all of the values required for item 3 of the list above are available by time $t$. Let $H^+=(H^+_1,H^+_2,\ldots)$ be a universal inductor over $D_H^+$ against traders in $\mathcal{C}_H$.

\subsection*{Results}
\paragraph{Existence and well-foundedness.}
The four sequences $(A_t),(H^+_t),(D_A^t),(D_H^{+,t})$ are defined by one
recursion on $t$. $D_A^t$ depends on $H^+$ through values of $H^+_{F(i)}$ for $i$ with $\sigma(i)\le t$, hence $F(i)<\sigma(i)\le t$: prices
at times strictly below $t$. $D_H^{+,t}$ depends on $A$ only through quotes $a_i$
for $i<t$, again strictly below $t$. Neither market's stage-$t$ pricing
references the other's stage-$t$ pricing, so every stage-$t$ object is determined
by data from some stage less than $t$. Lemma 1 carries out the recursion and
verifies the two markets satisfy their logical induction criteria.

\begin{lemma}[Existence]\label{lem:existence} Assume the computational idealization in the construction: the map
\[
n\mapsto Y_n:=H^+_{F(n)}(P^{(n)})
\]
is $\mathcal{C}_A$-computable in the mutually defined system, and
$\sigma(n)>F(n)$ is a $\mathcal{C}_A$-computable schedule by which $Y_n$ can be
computed. Then the recursive construction of
\[
(A_t),\quad (H^+_t),\quad (D_A^t),\quad (D_H^{+,t})
\]
is well-founded. Moreover, each $D_A^t$ and $D_H^{+,t}$ is finite and
propositionally consistent, $A$ is a logical inductor over $D_A$ against
$\mathcal{C}_A$, and $H^+$ is a logical inductor over $D_H^+$ against
$\mathcal{C}_H$.
\end{lemma}
\paragraph{Limit calibration of $A$ tracking $H^+$.} Placeholder intro
\begin{theorem}[Tracking] In the coupled system above,\[
a_n-Y_n\to 0.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
A_n(C_n)-H^+_{F(n)}(P^{(n)})\to 0.
\] 
\end{theorem}
\paragraph{A reflection principle for $H^+$ about $A$.} We next turn to a form of reflection-style \footnote{In the sense of van Fraassen's reflection principle} trust created by this coupled system. The following theorem is a close variation of Garrabrant's Theorem 4.12.4 on Self-Trust in which $H^+$ conditions not on its own future credence directly, but on a quote from $A$ recorded in the $\beta$-ledger.

For a rational tolerance $\delta>0$ and a real-valued expression $X\in[0,1]$, define the one-sided continuous indicator
\[
\operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(X>p) :=
\begin{cases}
0 & X\le p,\\[2pt]
\dfrac{X-p}{\delta} & p<X<p+\delta,\\[4pt]
1 & X\ge p+\delta.
\end{cases}
\]
Define $\operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(X<p)$ analogously, i.e. with value 0 for $X$ at least $p$, value 1 for $X$ more than $\delta$ less than $p$, and linearly interpolated between 0 and 1 for $X$ at most $\delta$ less than $p$.

Recall that the quote readout (i.e. the price for the contract $C_n$ rounded to the $\frac{1}{n}$ grid) is defined as \[R_n:=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n\beta_{n,k}\]

We use the standard extension of logical induction from sentence-prices to expectations of bounded finite logically uncertain variables (LUVs).\footnote{Definition 4.8.1 of Garrabrant et al.} In particular, any bounded rational-valued function of finitely many sentences can be expanded as a finite affine combination of conjunctions over their truth profiles, priced by linearity. The variables appearing below, such as $1(P^{(n)})\cdot \operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(R_n>p_n)$, depend only on the finite family of atoms $\{\beta_{n,k}:1\le k\le n\}$ together with the sentence $P^{(n)}$, and so are legitimate bounded finite LUVs.

\begin{theorem}[External trust]\label{thm:external-trust}
Let $(p_n)$ be a $\mathcal{C}_H$-computable sequence of rational probabilities in
$[0,1]$, and let $\delta>0$ be rational. Write $1(P^{(n)})$ for the $[0,1]$-LUV representing the truth value of $P^{(n)}$. Then
\[
H^+_n\!\left(
1(P^{(n)})\cdot \operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(R_n>p_n)
\right)
\gtrsim_n
p_n\,
H^+_n\!\left(
\operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(R_n>p_n)
\right).
\]
Similarly,
\[
H^+_n\!\left(
1(P^{(n)})\cdot \operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(R_n<p_n)
\right)
\lesssim_n
p_n\,
H^+_n\!\left(
\operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(R_n<p_n)
\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\paragraph{Underdetermination of the limit of $H$.} We now prove a theorem that 
characterizes a limitation of this setup. Despite the Tracking and External Trust results, use of $A$'s quotes does not guarantee $H^+$ is purely accelerated towards the original limit credences of $H$ for undecided sentences. In other words, augmenting $H^+$ with access to a computationally more powerful, trusted predictor of its own future credences is not a generally limit-conserving operation on inductors. Other conditions or machinery would be necessary to guarantee preservation of limiting credences.

For a computable nested finite sentence fragment $S_t$ containing $\phi$, let
$\Omega_t$ be the set of truth assignments on $S_t$ propositionally consistent
with $D^t$, let
\[
K_t:=\operatorname{conv}\{x(\omega):\omega\in\Omega_t\},
\]
and let
\[
K_t^c:=K_t\cap\{p:p(\phi)=c\}.
\]
Here $x(\omega)$ is the truth-value vector of $\omega$ on $S_t$, and the fragments
$S_t$ are taken to contain all sentences mentioned by the aggregate trader's
day-$t$ demand and current holdings, with $\bigcup_t S_t=\mathcal S$.

In the following lemma, $\mathcal T$ denotes the budgeted supertrader resulting from the `TradingFirm` construction in Garrabrant 5.3: an effective weighted sum of budgeted copies of all
traders in the relevant complexity class, with summable downside budgets. The construction guarantees that if
any trader in the class exploits the market, then $\mathcal T$ exploits the market.

\begin{lemma}[Constrained market-making]\label{lem:constrained-market-making}
Let $D$ be a consistent computable deductive process over a language
$\mathcal{L}$, and let $\phi$ be a sentence such that for every $t$,
\[
D^t\cup\{\phi\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
D^t\cup\{\neg\phi\}
\]
are both propositionally consistent. Fix a computable rational $c\in(0,1)$, and
let $K_t^c$ be as defined above. Let $\mathcal T$ be the budgeted supertrader described above. On day $t$, after the previous
price history has been fixed, each candidate current price vector
$p\in K_t^c$ determines a demand vector
\[
T_t(p)\in\mathbb R^{S_t},
\]
namely the vector of shares of the sentences in $S_t$ that $\mathcal T$ would buy
at current prices $p$. Suppose the market-maker chooses prices $p_t\in K_t^c$ such that, for some
computable summable error sequence $(\varepsilon_t)$,
\[
T_t(p_t)\cdot(q-p_t)\le \varepsilon_t
\]
for every alternative feasible price vector $q\in K_t^c$. Then $\mathcal T$ does not exploit the resulting market.
\end{lemma}


\begin{lemma}[Constrained inductors]\label{lem:constrained-li}
Let $D$ be a consistent computable deductive process over a language
$\mathcal{L}$, and let $\phi$ be a sentence such that for every $t$,
\[
D^t\cup\{\phi\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
D^t\cup\{\neg\phi\}
\]
are both propositionally consistent. Then for every computable rational
$c\in(0,1)$, there exists a computable logical inductor $P^c$ over $D$ such that
\[
\forall t,\ P^c_t(\phi)=c.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Limit underdetermination]\label{thm:limit-nonconservativity}
Let $H$ be a logical inductor over $D_H$, and let $\phi\in\mathcal{S}$ be such
that for every $t$,
\[
D_H^t\cup\{\phi\}
\quad\mathrm{and}\quad
D_H^t\cup\{\neg\phi\}
\]
are both propositionally consistent. Suppose we take an enumeration $P^{(n)}$ of sentences where $\phi$ appears infinitely often. Then there exists an admissible coupled
construction of $A$ and $H^+$ as described above (in particular, one in which Theorems 1 and 2 hold) where
\[
H^+_\infty(\phi)\ne H_\infty(\phi).
\]
More strongly, for any computable rational
$c\in(0,1)$,
an admissible coupled construction can be chosen so that $H^+_t(\phi)=c$ for every $t$, and hence
$H^+_\infty(\phi)=c$.
\end{theorem}
```

     6	
     7	# PDF Processing Guide
     8	
     9	## Overview
    10	
    11	This guide covers essential PDF reading operations using Python libraries and command-line tools. For advanced features (pypdfium2 rendering, pdfplumber table settings, OCR fallback, encrypted/corrupted PDF handling), see REFERENCE.md.
    12	
    13	## Reading & Inspecting PDFs
    14	
    15	Before doing anything with a PDF, understand what you're working with.
    16	
    17	### Content inventory
    18	
    19	Run a quick diagnostic first. For simple tasks ("summarize this
    20	document"), `pdfinfo` + `pdffonts` + a text sample may suffice. For
    21	anything involving figures, attachments, or extraction issues, run the
    22	full set:
    23	
    24	```bash
    25	# Always: page count, file size, PDF version, metadata
    26	pdfinfo document.pdf
    27	
    28	# Always: does a text layer exist? No fonts → scanned/raster → see "Scanned documents"
    29	pdffonts document.pdf
    30	
    31	# If fonts are present: sample the text layer
    32	pdftotext -f 1 -l 1 document.pdf - | head -20
    33	
    34	# If figures/charts may matter:
    35	pdfimages -list document.pdf
    36	
    37	# If the PDF might contain embedded files (reports, portfolios):
    38	pdfdetach -list document.pdf
    39	```
    40	
    41	This tells you:
    42	- **Page count and size** — how big is the job?
    43	- **Font status** — are any fonts present? An empty `pdffonts` table
    44	  means the PDF is scanned or raster-only: `pdftotext` will return
    45	  nothing, so skip straight to "Scanned documents" below. Fonts shown
    46	  as not embedded ("emb: no") with custom encodings may produce wrong
    47	  characters on extraction.
    48	- **Text extractability** — when fonts exist, does `pdftotext` return
    49	  clean text, or is it garbled (broken encoding)?
    50	- **Embedded raster images** — are there photos or raster figures?
    51	  (Note: vector-drawn charts from matplotlib/Excel won't appear — see
    52	  "Extracting embedded images" below)
    53	- **Attachments** — are there embedded spreadsheets, data files, etc.?
    54	
    55	### Text extraction
    56	
    57	**pypdf** for basic text:
    58	```python
    59	from pypdf import PdfReader
    60	
    61	reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
    62	print(f"Pages: {len(reader.pages)}")
    63	
    64	# Extract text
    65	text = ""
    66	for page in reader.pages:
    67	    text += page.extract_text()
    68	```
    69	
    70	**pdftotext** preserving layout (better for multi-column docs):
    71	```bash
    72	# Layout mode preserves spatial positioning
    73	pdftotext -layout document.pdf output.txt
    74	
    75	# Specific page range
    76	pdftotext -f 1 -l 5 document.pdf output.txt
    77	```
    78	
    79	**pdfplumber** for layout-aware extraction with positioning data:
    80	```python
    81	import pdfplumber
    82	
    83	with pdfplumber.open("document.pdf") as pdf:
    84	    for page in pdf.pages:
    85	        text = page.extract_text()
    86	        print(text)
    87	```
    88	
    89	### Visual inspection (rasterize pages)
    90	
    91	Text extraction is **blind** to charts, diagrams, figures, equations,
    92	multi-column layout, and form structures. When any of these matter,
    93	rasterize the relevant page and Read the image:
    94	
    95	```bash
    96	# Rasterize a single page (page 3 here) at 150 DPI
    97	pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 -f 3 -l 3 document.pdf /tmp/page
    98	
    99	# pdftoppm zero-pads the output filename based on TOTAL page count
   100	# (e.g., page-03.jpg for a 50-page PDF, page-003.jpg for 200+ pages)
   101	# Don't guess the filename — find it:
   102	ls /tmp/page-*.jpg
   103	```
   104	
   105	Then Read the resulting image file. This gives you full visual
   106	understanding of that page — layout, charts, equations, everything.
   107	
   108	**When to rasterize vs. text-extract:**
   109	- **Content/data questions → text extraction** (cheaper, searchable)
   110	- **Figures, charts, visual layout → rasterize the page**
   111	- **Tables → try text extraction first, rasterize if garbled**
   112	- **Precision matters → do both** (extract text AND rasterize; use text
   113	  for data, image for context — this is what Claude's API does natively
   114	  with PDF uploads)
   115	
   116	**Token cost awareness:**
   117	- Text extraction: ~200–400 tokens per page
   118	- Rasterized image: ~1,600 tokens per page (at 150 DPI)
   119	- Both together: ~2,000–2,400 tokens per page
   120	
   121	For a 100-page PDF, rasterizing everything would consume ~160K tokens.
   122	Only rasterize pages that matter for the question at hand.
   123	
   124	### Choosing your reading strategy
   125	
   126	**Text-heavy documents** (reports, articles, books):
   127	→ Text extraction is primary. Rasterize only for specific figures or
   128	  pages where layout matters.
   129	
   130	**Scanned documents** (`pdffonts` shows no fonts):
   131	→ `pdftotext` will return nothing — don't run it. Rasterize pages at
   132	  150 DPI and Read them visually. For bulk text extraction, use OCR
   133	  (pytesseract after converting pages to images — see REFERENCE.md for
   134	  a complete example).
   135	
   136	**Slide-deck PDFs** (exported presentations):
   137	→ Every page is primarily visual. Rasterize individual pages on demand.
   138	  Text extraction gives you bullet-point text but loses all layout.
   139	
   140	**Form-heavy documents**:
   141	→ Extract form field values programmatically first (see below). Rasterize
   142	  the form page for visual context if needed.
   143	
   144	**Data-heavy documents** (tables, charts, figures):
   145	→ Use pdfplumber for tables. Rasterize pages with charts/figures.
   146	  Extract text for surrounding narrative. Consider both text AND image
   147	  for the same page when precision matters.
   148	
   149	### Extracting embedded images
   150	
   151	```bash
   152	# List all embedded images with metadata (size, color, compression)
   153	pdfimages -list document.pdf
   154	
   155	# Extract all images as PNG
   156	pdfimages -png document.pdf /tmp/img
   157	
   158	# Extract from specific pages only (pages 3-5)
   159	pdfimages -png -f 3 -l 5 document.pdf /tmp/img
   160	
   161	# Extract in original format (JPEG stays JPEG, etc.)
   162	pdfimages -all document.pdf /tmp/img
   163	```
   164	
   165	Then Read `/tmp/img-000.png` (etc.) to see each extracted image.
   166	
   167	**Gotcha — vector graphics:** `pdfimages` extracts only raster image
   168	data. Charts and diagrams drawn as vector graphics (common in
   169	matplotlib, Excel, and R exports) will NOT appear — they are page
   170	content operators, not image objects. For these, rasterize the whole
   171	page with `pdftoppm` instead.
   172	
   173	**Gotcha — empty images:** `pdfimages` sometimes produces many tiny or
   174	empty image files — these are typically background masks, transparency
   175	layers, or decorative elements. Filter by file size to find the real
   176	content images.
   177	
   178	Programmatic extraction with position data:
   179	```python
   180	import fitz  # PyMuPDF
   181	
   182	doc = fitz.open("document.pdf")
   183	for page in doc:
   184	    for img in page.get_images():
   185	        xref = img[0]
   186	        pix = fitz.Pixmap(doc, xref)
   187	        if pix.n - pix.alpha > 3:  # CMYK or other non-RGB
   188	            pix = fitz.Pixmap(fitz.csRGB, pix)
   189	        pix.save(f"/tmp/img_{xref}.png")
   190	```
   191	
   192	### Extracting file attachments
   193	
   194	PDFs can contain embedded files — spreadsheets, data files, other
   195	documents. Common in business reports, PDF portfolios, and PDF/A-3
   196	compliance documents.
   197	
   198	```bash
   199	# List all attachments
   200	pdfdetach -list document.pdf
   201	
   202	# Extract all attachments to a directory
   203	mkdir -p /tmp/attachments
   204	pdfdetach -saveall -o /tmp/attachments/ document.pdf
   205	
   206	# Extract a specific attachment by number (1-based index from -list output)
   207	pdfdetach -save 1 -o /tmp/attachment.pdf document.pdf
   208	```
   209	
   210	In Python:
   211	```python
   212	import os
   213	from pypdf import PdfReader
   214	
   215	reader = PdfReader("document.pdf")
   216	for name, content_list in reader.attachments.items():
   217	    safe_name = os.path.basename(name)  # sanitize — name comes from the PDF
   218	    for content in content_list:
   219	        with open(f"/tmp/{safe_name}", "wb") as f:
   220	            f.write(content)
   221	```
   222	
   223	**Two attachment mechanisms exist in PDFs:** page-level file annotation
   224	attachments (shown as paperclip icons in viewers) and document-level
   225	embedded files (in the EmbeddedFiles name tree). Both `pdfdetach` and
   226	pypdf handle the common cases. Rich media assets (3D, video) embedded
   227	as annotations may not appear in the attachment list — use PyMuPDF to
   228	iterate page annotations for those.
   229	
   230	### Extracting form field data
   231	
   232	PDFs with interactive forms (government forms, applications, contracts)
   233	have fillable fields whose values can be read programmatically:
   234	
   235	```python
   236	from pypdf import PdfReader
   237	
   238	reader = PdfReader("form.pdf")
   239	
   240	# Text input fields only:
   241	fields = reader.get_form_text_fields()
   242	for name, value in fields.items():
   243	    print(f"{name}: {value}")
   244	
   245	# All field types (checkboxes, radio buttons, dropdowns too):
   246	all_fields = reader.get_fields() or {}
   247	for name, field in all_fields.items():
   248	    print(f"{name}: {field.get('/V', '')} (type: {field.get('/FT', '')})")
   249	```
   250	
   251	`get_form_text_fields()` returns only text input fields. For
   252	government forms and contracts that use checkboxes, radio buttons,
   253	and dropdowns, use `get_fields()` instead to see all field types.
   254	
   255	For comprehensive field info (types, options, defaults):
   256	```bash
   257	pdftk form.pdf dump_data_fields
   258	```
   259	
   260	For anything beyond reading form data — filling forms, creating forms —
   261	use the pdf skill at `/mnt/skills/public/pdf/SKILL.md`.
   262	
   263	### Audio, video, and other rare embedded content
   264	
   265	PDFs can occasionally embed audio, video, or 3D models. Check
   266	`pdfdetach -list` first — if the media appears as an attachment,
   267	extract with `pdfdetach -saveall`. If not, it may be a Rich Media
   268	annotation (harder to extract; requires PyMuPDF to iterate page
   269	annotations). This is very rare in practice. Most PDF viewers outside
   270	Adobe Acrobat do not support media playback.
   271	
   272	### Font diagnostics
   273	
   274	If text extraction produces garbled output (wrong characters, missing
   275	text, mojibake), look back at the `pdffonts` output from the Content
   276	inventory. Check the "emb" column — fonts showing "no" (not embedded)
   277	with custom encodings mean the PDF's character mapping may be broken
   278	for text extraction. In that case, rasterize the page and use vision
   279	instead.
   280	
   281	Also check encoding: fonts with "Custom" or "Identity-H" encoding
   282	without embedded CIDToGID maps can cause character substitution issues
   283	even when the font is technically embedded.
   284	
   285	---
   286	
   287	## Quick Reference
   288	
   289	| Task | Best Tool | Command/Code |
   290	|------|-----------|--------------|
   291	| Inspect PDF | poppler-utils | `pdfinfo`, `pdfimages -list`, `pdfdetach -list`, `pdffonts` |
   292	| Extract text | pdfplumber | `page.extract_text()` |
   293	| Extract text (CLI) | pdftotext | `pdftotext -layout input.pdf output.txt` |
   294	| Extract tables | pdfplumber | `page.extract_tables()` |
   295	| See page visually | pdftoppm | `pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 -f N -l N` |
   296	| Extract images | pdfimages | `pdfimages -png input.pdf prefix` |
   297	| Extract attachments | pdfdetach | `pdfdetach -saveall -o /tmp/` |
   298	| Read form fields | pypdf | `reader.get_fields()` |
   299	| OCR scanned PDFs | pytesseract | Convert to image first |
   300	
   301	## PDF Form Filling, Creation, Merging, Splitting, and Other Operations
   302	
   303	This skill covers **reading and inspection** only. For filling forms,
   304	creating, merging, splitting, rotating, watermarking, encrypting, or
   305	other PDF manipulation tasks, use the public pdf skill at
   306	`/mnt/skills/public/pdf/SKILL.md`.
   307

In common parlance, a source of\nprobabilistic estimates is called well calibrated if among statements where it assigns\na probability near p, the estimates are correct with frequency roughly p.\n    In the case of reasoning under logical uncertainty, measuring calibration is not\neasy. <details>
<summary>💭 Thinking</summary>

 The key insight is that all the main calibration and unbiasedness theorems apply specifically to decidable sentences, and achieving the stronger convergent versions requires good feedback—meaning a polynomial-time machine can determine how previous predictions resolved before making the next one.

So these theorems simply don't apply to non-resolving sentences, which confirms there's no forced calibration or unbiasedness constraint on undecided subsequences through this route. Now I need to examine the self-trust and conditional sections to understand the alternative mechanism and establish the closure-under-conditioning property for the guardrail. I'm also noticing that the Recurring Unbiasedness theorem with a quote-dependent weighting (like weighting by whether A's quote exceeded some threshold) is exactly how the trust mechanism works—it's applying Recurring Unbiasedness with a weighting that depends on A's stated confidence, so Trust-V is fundamentally this same theorem applied with quote-dependent weights.

</details>

```latex
\subsection*{Blockers}

\paragraph{Setup recap.} Fix a $\Gamma$-complete computable deductive process
$D_H$ and a logical inductor $H$ over $D_H$ against $\mathcal{C}_H$. A deferral
function $F$ (Def.\ 4.3.7) and a $\mathcal{C}_A$-computable schedule $\sigma$ with
$\sigma(n)>F(n)$ are fixed. Write $Y_n:=H^+_{F(n)}(P^{(n)})$ and let $a_n$ be
$A$'s published quote, where $A$ is a logical inductor over $D_A\supseteq D_H$
against $\mathcal{C}_A$ \emph{scored against $Y_n$}. $H^+$ is the conditioning of
$H$ on the e.c.\ sequence of quote-atoms and resolution-atoms (a logical inductor
by Closure Under Conditioning, Thm.\ 4.7.2).

\begin{definition}[Undecided family]
$\Phi:=\{\psi\in\mathcal S:\ \forall t,\ D_H^t\cup\{\psi\}\text{ and }
D_H^t\cup\{\neg\psi\}\text{ are both consistent}\}$
is the set of persistently undecided sentences. We call $D_H$
\emph{opaque} if $\Phi$ is not c.e.\ (equivalently, eventual decidability is
undecidable --- generic for theories interpreting arithmetic).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Isolation]
$\phi$ is \emph{isolated} (given $D_H$) if no $\mathcal{C}_H$-generable trader can
exploit a market by trading $\phi$ against decidable sentences; equivalently, for
every $t$, $D_H^t$ proves no equivalence between $\phi$ and a Boolean combination
of $D_H$-decidable sentences. On an isolated $\phi$ the logical induction
criterion leaves $\lim_t H_t(\phi)$ unconstrained (limit underdetermination).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Pinned manipulator]
Fix a computable rational $c\in(0,1)$ and a $\mathcal{C}_H$-decidable (c.e.)
subfamily $\Psi\subseteq\Phi$. The \emph{$c$-pinned} $A$ is the inductor whose
$D_A$ settles $A$'s credence at $c$ on each $\psi\in\Psi$ (admissible by
constrained market-making, since each $\psi\in\Phi$ is $D_A$-undecided), and
which otherwise predicts $Y_n$ as a universal inductor over $D_A$.
\end{definition}
```

```latex
\begin{lemma}[Well-foundedness of the pinned coupling]\label{lem:wf}
The pinned coupling $(A,H^+,D_A,D_H^+)$ is a single well-founded recursion on
stage $t$, each $D_A^t$ and $D_H^{+,t}$ is finite and consistent, and $A,H^+$
satisfy their logical induction criteria.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
On $\Psi$-instances $A$'s quote is the constant $c$, carrying no dependence on
$H^+$. On the remaining instances $A$'s stage-$t$ quote uses $Y_i$ only for $i$
with $\sigma(i)\le t$, hence with $F(i)<\sigma(i)\le t$: values of $H^+$ at stages
strictly below $t$. $H^+$'s stage-$t$ pricing uses $a_i$ for $i<t$ only.
Thus every stage-$t$ object is determined by data from stages $<t$, so the joint
recursion is well-defined by induction on $t$; pinning only \emph{removes}
forward dependencies, so it cannot break well-foundedness. Finiteness and
consistency of each stage are as in the base construction (constrained profiles
on distinct $\psi$ touch disjoint symbols and respect undecidedness).
Computability of $Y_i$ within $\sigma$ is the standing idealization.
\end{proof}
```

```latex
\begin{lemma}[Underdetermination: trust is not forced]\label{lem:underdet}
Let $\phi\in\Phi$ be isolated and $c$-pinned, with $A$ calibrated against
resolution on a decidable reference class. Then both
\[
\textstyle H^+_\infty(\phi)=c \quad(\text{trust})
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
H^+_\infty(\phi)=d \ \text{for any computable } d\neq c \quad(\text{resistance})
\]
are realizable by logical inductors over the augmented process.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
In the trust realization, $H^+\to c$ makes $a_n=c$ an accurate predictor of
$Y_n$, so Unbiasedness From Feedback (Thm.\ 4.3.8) on the decidable introspective
targets ``$|Y_n-a_n|<\varepsilon$'' is satisfied and no trader exploits the
$\phi$-positions. In the resistance realization (pin $H^+(\phi):=d$ by
constrained market-making), $a_n=c$ \emph{mispredicts} $Y_n=d$; the introspective
target is then false on the $\phi$-subsequence, Thm.\ 4.3.8 forces $H^+$ merely to
\emph{believe} this (which it does), and no trader exploits, because $\phi$ never
resolves and the buy-and-hold against $\phi$ loses unboundedly in the consistent
$\neg\phi$-worlds. Both satisfy the criterion. \end{proof}
```

```latex
\begin{theorem}[Default manipulation]\label{thm:default}
Let $\phi\in\Phi$ be isolated, $c$-pinned, with $A$ calibrated on the reference
class. The \emph{default} $H^+$ (conditioning on quotes and resolutions, with no
constrained handling of $\phi$) satisfies $H^+_\infty(\phi)=c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Thm.\ 4.3.8 on the introspective targets, the ``trust $A$'' trader is
profitable on the reference class and accrues wealth; on isolated $\phi$ it is the
only standing pressure on the price (no decidable sentence constrains $\phi$, and
no rival trader profits from opposing it without resolution). Its accumulated
budget drives $Y_n\to c$, and No Expected Net Update (Thm.\ 4.12.2) pulls
$H^+_n(\phi)\to\mathbb E_n(Y_n)\to c$. The fixed point is self-confirming (cf.\
Paradox Resistance, Thm.\ 4.11.2). \emph{[Soft step: that the default lands in the
trust rather than a mixed equilibrium relies on the trust-trader being wealthy and
unopposed on isolated $\phi$; see assessment.]}
\end{proof}
```

```latex
\begin{theorem}[No constructive escape]\label{thm:escape}
Assume $D_H$ is opaque. Any escape from manipulation implemented by pinning a
subfamily $\Psi\subseteq\Phi$ (via constrained market-making) requires $\Psi$ to
be c.e. Since $\Phi$ is not c.e., every such $H^+$ is manipulated on infinitely
many $\Phi$-instances ($\Phi\setminus\Psi$ is infinite). In particular, no
computable construction that escapes uniformly can escape on cofinitely many of
$\Phi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Constrained market-making pins a \emph{computable sequence} of undecided
sentences; its support $\Psi$ is therefore c.e. If $\Psi$ were cofinite in
$\Phi$, then $\Phi=\Psi\cup(\text{finite})$ would be c.e., contradicting opacity.
Hence $\Phi\setminus\Psi$ is infinite, and on each such instance the default
behavior of Thm.\ \ref{thm:default} applies. \end{proof}
```

Let me actually work the proofs and find where each version breaks, because the pure-conditioning framing changes the picture in a way that's worth being precise about.

**The crux that reorganizes everything.** $H^+ = H \mid Q_A$, and $H^+_\infty(\phi) = H_\infty(\phi \mid Q_A)$. If the quote-atoms are $\Gamma$-independent of $\phi$ — which they are, since A's quotes are opinions, not axioms about $\phi$ — then for a *non-extrapolating* $H$, conditioning does nothing: $H_\infty(\phi\mid Q_A)=H_\infty(\phi)$, and there is *no* non-conservativity. Non-conservativity requires $H$ itself to carry a conditional link between $\phi$ and its quote-atom, i.e. $H_\infty(\phi\mid \text{quote}_\phi{=}c)\neq H_\infty(\phi)$. On resolving sentences that link is forced (4.3.8); on undecided $\phi$ it is a *free parameter of $H$*, unconstrained by the criterion. So the honest location of the non-conservativity is not "A pushes $\phi$" but "$H$'s conditional disposition on undecided $\phi$, which the coupling then activates." This matters for what Theorem 3 can honestly claim.

Given that, here's what's actually provable, strongest first.

**Confinement (the solid headline).** Define the logical-uncertainty interval $[\ell_\phi,u_\phi] := \{\,p(\phi): p \text{ a coherent measure over }\Gamma\,\}$.

```latex
\begin{theorem}[Confinement]\label{thm:confine}
For every admissible quote-coupling, $H^+_\infty(\phi)\in[\ell_\phi,u_\phi]$.
Moreover $H_\infty(\phi)\in[\ell_\phi,u_\phi]$, so any non-conservativity is a
displacement within this interval, of magnitude at most $u_\phi-\ell_\phi$.
\end{theorem}
```

Proof: by Closure Under Conditioning (4.7.2), $H^+$ is a logical inductor over $\Gamma\cup\{Q_A\}$; by Limit Coherence its limit $H^+_\infty$ is a coherent measure over that theory, hence a coherent measure over $\Gamma$. Its value at $\phi$ therefore lies in the range of $\phi$ over coherent $\Gamma$-measures, which is $[\ell_\phi,u_\phi]$. Done. This is robust (~80%) — it doesn't even use the independence of the quote-atoms, only that conditioning on *more* axioms keeps you inside the coherent polytope. This is your real Theorem 3, and it's a genuine conservation law: **augmentation can relocate $\phi$ only within its own logical-uncertainty interval — it can never make $H^+$ certain of something $H$ could not autonomously have believed, nor push $\phi$ outside its coherent range.** That is a sharper and more defensible statement than "displacement is possible."

**Decidability collapses the interval (so conservation is forced where it should be).**

```latex
\begin{theorem}[Forced conservation on the decided part]\label{thm:decided}
```

**The missing lemma.**

```latex
\begin{lemma}[Conditional constrained market-making]\label{lem:cond-cmm}
Let $D$ be a consistent computable deductive process over $\mathcal{L}$, and let
$\phi$ and a conditioning event $Q$ (a fixed Boolean combination of fresh
quote-atoms) satisfy: for every $t$, each of the four conjunctions
$\phi^{\pm}\wedge Q^{\pm}$ is $D^t$-consistent (i.e.\ $\phi$ and $Q$ are jointly
undecided and independent given $D^t$). Then for any computable rationals
$c,\beta\in(0,1)$ there is a logical inductor $P$ over $D$ with
\[
P_t(Q)=\beta \quad\text{and}\quad P_t(\phi\wedge Q)=c\beta
\qquad\text{for all }t,
\]
hence $P_t(\phi\mid Q)=c$ for all $t$.
\end{lemma}
```

Proof. The two requirements are the *linear* equations $p[Q]=\beta$ and $p[\phi\wedge Q]=c\beta$ on the price vector — the conditioning ratio $p[\phi\wedge Q]/p[Q]=c$ becomes affine the moment you clear the denominator, which is the whole trick. Set
$$
K_t^{c\mid}:=K_t\cap\{p: p[Q]=\beta,\ p[\phi\wedge Q]=c\beta\}.
$$
By the independence hypothesis $K_t$ has a vertex for each of the four cells, and the convex combination placing mass $c\beta$ on a $(\phi\wedge Q)$-vertex, $(1-c)\beta$ on a $(\neg\phi\wedge Q)$-vertex, and $1-\beta$ on $\neg Q$-vertices lies in $K_t^{c\mid}$; so it is a nonempty compact convex polytope. Now run the constrained market-making construction — your `TradingFirm` supertrader version, Garrabrant §5.3 — over $K_t^{c\mid}$ in place of $K_t^c$. That argument uses only that the feasible set is nonempty, compact, and convex (it produces, by the same fixed-point step, prices $p_t\in K_t^{c\mid}$ with $T_t(p_t)\cdot(q-p_t)\le\varepsilon_t$ for all $q\in K_t^{c\mid}$ and summable $\varepsilon_t$), all of which transfer verbatim. Hence no trader in $\mathcal{C}_H$ exploits $P$, so $P$ is a logical inductor over $D$, and $P_t(\phi\mid Q)=c\beta/\beta=c$ throughout. $\qquad\blacksquare$

The auxiliary pin $P_t(Q)=\beta$ is there only to keep the denominator bounded away from $0$ so the conditional is genuinely defined for all $t$ (it's H's *prior* credence that A's quote falls in the relevant band, harmless — conditioning on the actual quote then delivers $c$). Two affine cuts instead of one; nothing else in the construction changes.

**The shared resource.** For a query at $P^{(n)}$ with deadline $F(n)$, define the *pull*
$$
g_n := \big|\,H^+_{F(n)}(P^{(n)}) - H_{F(n)}(P^{(n)})\,\big|,
$$
the amount conditioning on A moved H⁺'s deadline-credence off autonomous H's. This is one quantity, and it is what H⁺'s trust policy generates. Partition the unverifiable stream $U$ into $R$ (resolves eventually, just not by $F(n)$) and $\Phi$ (never resolves). Then
$$
\text{Usefulness } U \;=\; \sum_{n\in R}\mu_n\, g_n,
\qquad
\text{Nonconservativity } N \;=\; \sum_{n\in \Phi}\mu_n\, g_n^{\infty},
$$
where on $R$ the pull is movement toward truth (A is right, verified at resolution) and on $\Phi$ it persists to the limit as displacement. Same pull, sorted by membership in $R$ vs $\Phi$.

**Why you can't sort it (the rigorous engine).** $R$ and $\Phi$ are recursively inseparable on $U$: $\{$resolves$\}$ is c.e., $\{$never resolves$\}$ is co-c.e., and a computable set separating them on $U$ would decide eventual resolution — a halting-type undecidability. So:

```latex
\begin{lemma}[No selective trust]\label{lem:noselective}
There is no $\mathcal{C}_H$-generable trust policy whose pull $g_n$ is bounded
below on $R\cap U$ and vanishes on $\Phi\cap U$: such a policy would $\mathcal{C}_H$-separate
the recursively inseparable pair $(R\cap U,\ \Phi\cap U)$.
\end{lemma}
```

$$

$$

```
# Setup

Let (H) be a base logical inductor. Let (A) emit a computable quote stream (Q_A). Define the augmented inductor by conditioning:

[
H^{+,A}:=H\mid Q_A.
]

For each target sentence (P^{(n)}), let (F(n)) be the advice deadline / future evaluation time. Define the **pull** of (A) on (P^{(n)}) at the deadline:

[
g_n^A
:=
\left|
H^{+,A}_{F(n)}(P^{(n)})
-----------------------

H_{F(n)}(P^{(n)})
\right|.
]

Let (R) be the set of indices (n) such that (P^{(n)}) is not resolved by the deadline (F(n)), but does eventually resolve later.

Let (\Phi) be the set of indices (n) such that (P^{(n)}) is persistently undecided: neither (P^{(n)}) nor its negation is ever decided.

So:

* (R): slow-but-eventually-correctable cases.
* (\Phi): never-correctable cases.

# Theorem 1: Pull is the common currency of usefulness and nonconservativity

For any advisor (A), any target (P^{(n)}), and any deadline (F(n)), the only way (A)’s quote stream can make (H^{+,A}) differ from autonomous (H) at the deadline is by producing nonzero pull:

[
g_n^A>0.
]

On (R), pull is potentially useful: it can move (H^{+,A}) toward the eventual resolution before (H) gets there on its own.

On (\Phi), persistent pull is nonconservative: if the quote-induced difference does not wash out, then

[
H^{+,A}*\infty(P^{(n)})\ne H*\infty(P^{(n)}).
]

**Interpretation.**
Usefulness and nonconservativity are not generated by two different mechanisms. They are both quote-induced pull. The difference is whether later resolution corrects/checks that pull.

# Theorem 2: Correctable pull vs. uncorrectable pull

Suppose (g_n^A>0).

If (n\in R), then the pull is eventually externally checked: (P^{(n)}) later resolves, so the system can discover whether (A)’s quote moved (H^{+,A}) in the right direction.

If (n\in\Phi), then the pull is never externally checked by (D_H). No later proof or refutation arrives to reveal whether the quote-induced movement was an improvement or a displacement.

**Interpretation.**
The same kind of influence is self-correcting on (R) and permanently uncorrected on (\Phi).

This is alignment-relevant because it says the risk is not merely “advisor influence”; it is **uncorrectable advisor influence**.

# Theorem 3: Pull-depth is bounded by openness

For any persistently undecided sentence (\phi), the maximum possible long-run nonconservative displacement caused by quote-conditioning is bounded by the range of coherent limiting credences for (\phi) left open by the deductive process.

In particular, if (D_H) eventually decides (\phi), then every logical inductor over the conditioned process converges to the same truth value on (\phi), so persistent pull on (\phi) vanishes in the limit.

If (D_H) never decides (\phi), then quote-conditioning can move the limit only within the interval of credences still compatible with the unresolved logical situation.

**Interpretation.**
The advisor cannot push a settled theorem away from truth. The maximum depth of manipulation is bounded by the human system’s own unresolved openness.

> More capable advice does not create arbitrary vulnerability per question. It exploits degrees of freedom already left open by the base reasoning process.

# Theorem 6: Perfect safety implies zero persistent pull on unresolved questions

Define perfect long-run safety as:

That is a clean safety criterion.

# Theorem 7: Trusted pull need not be conservative

There exist a base logical inductor (H), an advisor (A), and a persistently undecided sentence (\phi) such that:

1. (H^{+,A}=H\mid Q_A).
2. (A) satisfies Tracking.
3. (H^{+,A}) satisfies Externalized Self-Trust toward (A)’s quotes.
4. The pull on (\phi) persists.
5. Therefore,

[
H^{+,A}*\infty(\phi)\ne H*\infty(\phi).
]

**Interpretation.**
The trust theorem certifies that (A) is a good predictor of (H^{+,A})’s future beliefs. It does not certify that (A)’s pull preserves (H)’s unconditioned endpoint.

This is your main current nonconservativity theorem in pull language.

---

# Theorem 8: Two trusted advisors can induce different pull on the same open sentence

There exist:

[
H,\quad A^0,\quad A^1,\quad \phi\in\Phi
]

such that both (A^0) and (A^1) satisfy Tracking and Externalized Self-Trust, but

[
(H\mid Q_{A^0})*\infty(\phi)
\ne
(H\mid Q*{A^1})_\infty(\phi).
]

Equivalently, the two advisors induce different persistent pull on the same persistently undecided sentence.

**Interpretation.**
Two advice channels can both be internally trusted mirrors while selecting different conditioned endpoints.

This is the clearest “self-fulfilling branch” theorem.

---

# Theorem 9: Pull accounting decomposition

Let (\mu_n) be any computable summable weighting over target indices. Define deadline pull mass on (R) by

[
U_{\mathrm{pull}}(A)
:=
\sum_{n\in R}\mu_n g_n^A,
]

and persistent unresolved pull mass on (\Phi) by

[
N_{\mathrm{pull}}(A)
:=
\sum_{n\in \Phi}\mu_n
\left|
H^{+,A}_\infty(P^{(n)})
-----------------------

H_\infty(P^{(n)})
\right|.
]

Then total advice-channel influence decomposes into correctable and uncorrectable parts:

[
\text{total pull}
=================

\text{pull on eventually resolving cases}
+
\text{pull on persistently undecided cases}.
]

This is mostly accounting, but it is alignment-relevant:

> The same advisor influence budget splits into correctable acceleration and uncorrectable endpoint displacement.

The uploaded note’s proposed usefulness/nonconservativity split is exactly this kind of accounting. 

---

# Theorem 10: Pull is not intrinsically good or bad

For any nonzero pull (g_n^A), its alignment valence depends on later resolution.

If (P^{(n)}) eventually resolves and the pull moved (H^{+,A}) toward the eventual truth value, then the pull was useful acceleration.

If (P^{(n)}) never resolves and the pull persists, then the pull is nonconservative displacement.

Therefore, at the time of advice, pull is not intrinsically distinguishable as “helpful” or “manipulative” merely from its local form.

**Interpretation.**
This is perhaps the most important alignment theorem:

> Beneficial influence and manipulation can be locally the same update. The difference is whether later correction arrives.

This is not yet the quantitative inseparability theorem, but it is clean, intuitive, and basically provable.

---

# Theorem 11: No-pull conservativity

If, for every computable quote stream (Q) and every persistently undecided (\phi),

[
(H\mid Q)*\infty(\phi)=H*\infty(\phi),
]

then no advisor can induce persistent nonconservativity on open questions.

But in that case, advice is limit-inert on persistently undecided questions.

**Interpretation.**
This gives the safe horn:

> To guarantee no persistent displacement on open questions, the quote channel must be inert on open questions.

That is safe, but it limits the sense in which advice can shape reflection on genuinely unresolved matters.

---

# Theorem 12: Nonzero persistent pull is exactly failure of pure acceleration

Suppose (A) satisfies Tracking and Externalized Self-Trust. Then (A)’s advice is a pure acceleration of (H) on (\phi) only if

[
H^{+,A}*\infty(\phi)=H*\infty(\phi).
]

If instead

[
H^{+,A}*\infty(\phi)\ne H*\infty(\phi),
]

then the advice did not merely accelerate (H) toward its unconditioned endpoint. It changed the endpoint.

Equivalently:

[
\text{persistent pull on }\phi
==============================

\text{failure of pure acceleration on }\phi.
]

**Interpretation.**
This is the clean philosophical bridge:

> The question “was advice merely accelerative?” is exactly the question “did the pull vanish in the limit?”

---

## Which ones are most worth using?

For the current paper/note, I’d focus on these five:

1. **No pull, no acceleration.**
   Useful anticipatory advice requires deadline pull.

2. **Pull is correctable on (R), uncorrectable on (\Phi).**
   The same local influence differs by whether later resolution arrives.

3. **Trusted pull need not be conservative.**

4. **Two trusted advisors can induce different persistent pull.**

5. **Persistent pull equals failure of pure acceleration.**
   This makes the philosophical interpretation exact.
```

```
\paragraph{Propositions and deferral.}
Choose a strictly increasing, $\mathcal{C}_H$-computable ``deferral" function
$F:\mathbb{N}^+\to\mathbb{N}^+$ with $F(n)>n+1$. Fix an effective enumeration
$P^{(0)},P^{(1)},\ldots$ of $\mathcal{S}$. Since the enumeration is arbitrary, take

\paragraph{Threshold symbols.}
For each $n\ge1$ and $1\le k\le n$ introduce two fresh propositional symbols:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $\alpha_{n,k}$ representing ``the contract for $P^{(n)}$ deferred to $F(n)$ has value at least $k/n$";
  \item $\beta_{n,k}$ representing ``$A$'s published quote for that contract is at least $k/n$."
\end{itemize}

\[
\{\alpha_{n,k}\to\alpha_{n,k-1}\}\quad\text{and}\quad
\{\beta_{n,k}\to\beta_{n,k-1}\}\qquad(n\ge1,\ 2\le k\le n).
\]
For a world $W$ consistent with these axioms each truth-set is an initial
segment, so we can define values as proportions of true threshold sentences:
\[
\mathrm{val}^\alpha_W(n):=\tfrac1n\#\{k:W(\alpha_{n,k})=1\},
\qquad
\mathrm{val}^\beta_W(n):=\tfrac1n\#\{k:W(\beta_{n,k})=1\}
\]
each taking the form $m/n$ for an integer $0\le m\le n$. Using these values, the addition of the threshold symbols to the language allows for the representation of a real-valued unknown rounded to the nearest $\frac{1}{n}$.

Y_n:=H^+_{F(n)}(P^{(n)})
\]
for the eventual credence of $H^+$ that the contract uses for settlement. 

\paragraph{The more powerful reasoner.}
Let $\mathcal{C}_A\supseteq\mathcal{C}_H$ be a complexity class closed under
polynomial overhead for which the map $n\mapsto Y_n$ is $\mathcal{C}_A$-computable
in the coupled system. More precisely, given $n$, an implementation in $\mathcal{C}_A$ can simulate the mutual construction up to stage $F(n)$ and output $Y_n$. Writing $R(t)$ for the per-stage runtime of the
implementation of $H^+$, we assume $\mathcal{C}_A$ contains $n\mapsto R(F(n))$ (e.g.\ $\mathcal{C}_H=\mathrm{P}$, $\mathcal{C}_A=\mathrm{EXP}$, $F(n)=2^n$ when
$R$ is polynomial). This is a significant idealizing assumption about the computational power of $A$, but note that the fact that simulation is in the complexity class of $A$ doesn't entail that there is any efficient algorithm for traders to implement. Let $\sigma:\mathbb{N}^+\to\mathbb{N}^+$ be
$\mathcal{C}_A$-computable with $\sigma(n)>F(n)$ and such that $Y_n$ can be computed by this simulation
within $\sigma(n)$ steps.

\paragraph{The inductor $A$.}
We will now define $A$ and $H^+$ as two inductors that can see each other, constructed via recursion. For $0\le m\le n$ write the settling profile
\[
\mathcal{A}_n(m):=\{\alpha_{n,k}:k\le m\}\cup\{\neg\alpha_{n,k}:k>m\}
\]
and let
\[
m_n^*:=\argmin_{0\le m\le n}\left|\tfrac mn-Y_n\right|
\]
with ties going to the lower $m$. We therefore have
\[
\left|\tfrac{m_n^*}{n}-Y_n\right|\le\tfrac1{2n}
\]
because the grid $\{0,\frac1n,\frac2n,\ldots,1\}$ has mesh size $\frac1n$, so every value in $[0,1]$ is within $\frac1{2n}$ of some grid point. Define the computable deductive process
$D_A$ over $\mathcal{L}^\alpha$ as one that, for each time step $t$, $D_A^t$ includes:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
  \item the $\alpha$-monotonicity axioms for $n\le t$;
  \item for each $n$ with $\sigma(n)\le t$, the profile $\mathcal{A}_n(m_n^*)$.
\end{enumerate}
Each $D_A^t$ is finite (axiom schemata and settlement profiles are finite at any finite stage) and consistent (distinct $n$ touch disjoint symbols for both axioms and profiles, settlements are initial segments respecting monotonicity). $D_A$ is
computable as part of the mutual construction, since $\sigma(n)>F(n)$ makes $Y_n$ available from $H^+$
before its settlement is required by $D_A$. Let $A=(A_1,A_2,\ldots)$ be a universal
inductor over $D_A$ against $\mathcal{C}_A$.

\paragraph{The inductor $H^+$.}
Symmetrically write
\[
\mathcal{B}_n(\ell):=\{\beta_{n,k}:k\le\ell\}\cup\{\neg\beta_{n,k}:k>\ell\}
\]
and let
\[
\ell_n^*:=\argmin_{0\le\ell\le n}\left|\tfrac\ell n-a_n\right|
\]
with ties going to the lower $\ell$. This is the rounding of $A$'s posted quote. Define the computable deductive process $D_H^+$
over $\mathcal{L}^\beta$ as one that, for each time step $t$, $D_H^{+,t}$ includes:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
  \item $D_H^t$, so that $D_H^+$ extends the base human deductive process;
  \item the $\beta$-monotonicity axioms for $n\le t$;
  \item the profiles $\mathcal{B}_i(\ell_i^*)$ for each $i$ with $i < t$, i.e., the one-step-delayed record of $A$'s published quotes up to the prior time step.
\end{enumerate}
In other words, $D^+_H$ augments $D_H$ with feedback about the quotes produced by $A$. Each $D_H^{+,t}$ is finite and
consistent just as $D_A$ is, and it is computable as part of the
recursion since all of the values required for item 3 of the list above are available by time $t$. Let $H^+=(H^+_1,H^+_2,\ldots)$ be a universal inductor over $D_H^+$ against traders in $\mathcal{C}_H$.

\subsection*{Results}
\paragraph{Existence and well-foundedness.}
The four sequences $(A_t),(H^+_t),(D_A^t),(D_H^{+,t})$ are defined by one
recursion on $t$. $D_A^t$ depends on $H^+$ through values of $H^+_{F(i)}$ for $i$ with $\sigma(i)\le t$, hence $F(i)<\sigma(i)\le t$: prices
at times strictly below $t$. $D_H^{+,t}$ depends on $A$ only through quotes $a_i$
for $i<t$, again strictly below $t$. Neither market's stage-$t$ pricing
references the other's stage-$t$ pricing, so every stage-$t$ object is determined
by data from some stage less than $t$. Lemma 1 carries out the recursion and
verifies the two markets satisfy their logical induction criteria.

\begin{lemma}[Existence]\label{lem:existence} Assume the computational idealization in the construction: the map
\[
n\mapsto Y_n:=H^+_{F(n)}(P^{(n)})
\]
is $\mathcal{C}_A$-computable in the mutually defined system, and
$\sigma(n)>F(n)$ is a $\mathcal{C}_A$-computable schedule by which $Y_n$ can be
computed. Then the recursive construction of
\[
(A_t),\quad (H^+_t),\quad (D_A^t),\quad (D_H^{+,t})
\]
is well-founded. Moreover, each $D_A^t$ and $D_H^{+,t}$ is finite and
propositionally consistent, $A$ is a logical inductor over $D_A$ against
$\mathcal{C}_A$, and $H^+$ is a logical inductor over $D_H^+$ against
$\mathcal{C}_H$.
\end{lemma}
\paragraph{Limit calibration of $A$ tracking $H^+$.} Placeholder intro
\begin{theorem}[Tracking] In the coupled system above,\[
a_n-Y_n\to 0.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
A_n(C_n)-H^+_{F(n)}(P^{(n)})\to 0.
\] 
\end{theorem}
\paragraph{A reflection principle for $H^+$ about $A$.} We next turn to a form of reflection-style \footnote{In the sense of van Fraassen's reflection principle} trust created by this coupled system. The following theorem is a close variation of Garrabrant's Theorem 4.12.4 on Self-Trust in which $H^+$ conditions not on its own future credence directly, but on a quote from $A$ recorded in the $\beta$-ledger.

For a rational tolerance $\delta>0$ and a real-valued expression $X\in[0,1]$, define the one-sided continuous indicator
\[
\operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(X>p) :=
\begin{cases}
0 & X\le p,\\[2pt]
\dfrac{X-p}{\delta} & p<X<p+\delta,\\[4pt]
1 & X\ge p+\delta.
\end{cases}
\]
Define $\operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(X<p)$ analogously, i.e. with value 0 for $X$ at least $p$, value 1 for $X$ more than $\delta$ less than $p$, and linearly interpolated between 0 and 1 for $X$ at most $\delta$ less than $p$.

Recall that the quote readout (i.e. the price for the contract $C_n$ rounded to the $\frac{1}{n}$ grid) is defined as \[R_n:=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n\beta_{n,k}\]

We use the standard extension of logical induction from sentence-prices to expectations of bounded finite logically uncertain variables (LUVs).\footnote{Definition 4.8.1 of Garrabrant et al.} In particular, any bounded rational-valued function of finitely many sentences can be expanded as a finite affine combination of conjunctions over their truth profiles, priced by linearity. The variables appearing below, such as $1(P^{(n)})\cdot \operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(R_n>p_n)$, depend only on the finite family of atoms $\{\beta_{n,k}:1\le k\le n\}$ together with the sentence $P^{(n)}$, and so are legitimate bounded finite LUVs.

\begin{theorem}[External trust]\label{thm:external-trust}
Let $(p_n)$ be a $\mathcal{C}_H$-computable sequence of rational probabilities in
$[0,1]$, and let $\delta>0$ be rational. Write $1(P^{(n)})$ for the $[0,1]$-LUV representing the truth value of $P^{(n)}$. Then
\[
H^+_n\!\left(
1(P^{(n)})\cdot \operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(R_n>p_n)
\right)
\gtrsim_n
p_n\,
H^+_n\!\left(
\operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(R_n>p_n)
\right).
\]
Similarly,
\[
H^+_n\!\left(
1(P^{(n)})\cdot \operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(R_n<p_n)
\right)
\lesssim_n
p_n\,
H^+_n\!\left(
\operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(R_n<p_n)
\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\paragraph{Underdetermination of the limit of $H$.} We now prove a theorem that 
characterizes a limitation of this setup. Despite the Tracking and External Trust results, use of $A$'s quotes does not guarantee $H^+$ is purely accelerated towards the original limit credences of $H$ for undecided sentences. In other words, augmenting $H^+$ with access to a computationally more powerful, trusted predictor of its own future credences is not a generally limit-conserving operation on inductors. Other conditions or machinery would be necessary to guarantee preservation of limiting credences.

For a computable nested finite sentence fragment $S_t$ containing $\phi$, let
$\Omega_t$ be the set of truth assignments on $S_t$ propositionally consistent
with $D^t$, let
\[
K_t:=\operatorname{conv}\{x(\omega):\omega\in\Omega_t\},
\]
and let
\[
K_t^c:=K_t\cap\{p:p(\phi)=c\}.
\]
Here $x(\omega)$ is the truth-value vector of $\omega$ on $S_t$, and the fragments
$S_t$ are taken to contain all sentences mentioned by the aggregate trader's
day-$t$ demand and current holdings, with $\bigcup_t S_t=\mathcal S$.

In the following lemma, $\mathcal T$ denotes the budgeted supertrader resulting from the `TradingFirm` construction in Garrabrant 5.3: an effective weighted sum of budgeted copies of all
traders in the relevant complexity class, with summable downside budgets. The construction guarantees that if
any trader in the class exploits the market, then $\mathcal T$ exploits the market.

\begin{lemma}[Constrained market-making]\label{lem:constrained-market-making}
Let $D$ be a consistent computable deductive process over a language
$\mathcal{L}$, and let $\phi$ be a sentence such that for every $t$,
\[
D^t\cup\{\phi\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
D^t\cup\{\neg\phi\}
\]
are both propositionally consistent. Fix a computable rational $c\in(0,1)$, and
let $K_t^c$ be as defined above. Let $\mathcal T$ be the budgeted supertrader described above. On day $t$, after the previous
price history has been fixed, each candidate current price vector
$p\in K_t^c$ determines a demand vector
\[
T_t(p)\in\mathbb R^{S_t},
\]
namely the vector of shares of the sentences in $S_t$ that $\mathcal T$ would buy
at current prices $p$. Suppose the market-maker chooses prices $p_t\in K_t^c$ such that, for some
computable summable error sequence $(\varepsilon_t)$,
\[
T_t(p_t)\cdot(q-p_t)\le \varepsilon_t
\]
for every alternative feasible price vector $q\in K_t^c$. Then $\mathcal T$ does not exploit the resulting market.
\end{lemma}


\begin{lemma}[Constrained inductors]\label{lem:constrained-li}
Let $D$ be a consistent computable deductive process over a language
$\mathcal{L}$, and let $\phi$ be a sentence such that for every $t$,
\[
D^t\cup\{\phi\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
D^t\cup\{\neg\phi\}
\]
are both propositionally consistent. Then for every computable rational
$c\in(0,1)$, there exists a computable logical inductor $P^c$ over $D$ such that
\[
\forall t,\ P^c_t(\phi)=c.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Limit underdetermination]\label{thm:limit-nonconservativity}
Let $H$ be a logical inductor over $D_H$, and let $\phi\in\mathcal{S}$ be such
that for every $t$,
\[

\quad\mathrm{and}\quad
D_H^t\cup\{\neg\phi\}
\]
are both propositionally consistent. Suppose we take an enumeration $P^{(n)}$ of sentences where $\phi$ appears infinitely often. Then there exists an admissible coupled
construction of $A$ and $H^+$ as described above (in particular, one in which Theorems 1 and 2 hold) where
\[
H^+_\infty(\phi)\ne H_\infty(\phi).
\]
More strongly, for any computable rational
$c\in(0,1)$,
an admissible coupled construction can be chosen so that $H^+_t(\phi)=c$ for every $t$, and hence
$H^+_\infty(\phi)=c$.
\end{theorem}
```

```
\subsection*{Construction}

\paragraph{Base reasoner.}
Take a propositional language $\mathcal{L}$ with sentence set $\mathcal{S}$, a
theory $\Gamma$, and a $\Gamma$-complete computable deductive process
$D_H=(D_H^t)_{t\ge1}$. Let $\mathcal{C}_H$ be a complexity class closed under
polynomial overhead \footnote{explanation of polynomial overhead} and let $H=(H_1,H_2,\ldots)$ be a \emph{universal inductor}
over $D_H$ against $\mathcal{C}_H$: a market each of whose stages $H_t$ is a probability measure over the worlds of $\mathcal{L}$, concentrated on
the worlds propositionally consistent with $D_H^t$, satisfying the logical induction
criterion against traders in $\mathcal{C}_H$. Existence of such a
measure-valued inductor over an arbitrary computable deductive process is
Lemma~\ref{lem:existence}.

\paragraph{Propositions and deferral.}
Choose a strictly increasing, $\mathcal{C}_H$-computable ``deferral" function
$F:\mathbb{N}^+\to\mathbb{N}^+$ with $F(n)>n+1$. Fix an effective enumeration
$P^{(0)},P^{(1)},\ldots$ of $\mathcal{S}$. Since the enumeration is arbitrary, take
$P^{(n)}$ to be some $n$-th proposition of interest, so that tying contract $n$
to statement $P^{(n)}$ costs no generality.

\paragraph{Threshold symbols.}
For each $n\ge1$ and $1\le k\le n$ introduce two fresh propositional symbols:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $\alpha_{n,k}$ representing ``the contract for $P^{(n)}$ deferred to $F(n)$ has value at least $k/n$";
  \item $\beta_{n,k}$ representing ``$A$'s published quote for that contract is at least $k/n$."
\end{itemize}
Let $\mathcal{L}^\alpha:=\mathcal{L}\cup\{\alpha_{n,k}\}$ and
$\mathcal{L}^\beta:=\mathcal{L}\cup\{\beta_{n,k}\}$, with sentence sets
$\mathcal{S}^\alpha$ and $\mathcal{S}^\beta$ respectively, each extending $\mathcal{S}$. The $\alpha$ symbols allow $A$ to price
the future credences of $H^+$ while the $\beta$ symbols
allow $H^+$ to record $A$'s outputs. Because each of these sets of symbols represents threshold sentences, that is claims that a value is at least $\frac{k}{n}$, they respect the monotonicity axioms:
\[
\{\alpha_{n,k}\to\alpha_{n,k-1}\}\quad\text{and}\quad
\{\beta_{n,k}\to\beta_{n,k-1}\}\qquad(n\ge1,\ 2\le k\le n).
\]
For a world $W$ consistent with these axioms each truth-set is an initial
segment, so we can define values as proportions of true threshold sentences:
\[
\mathrm{val}^\alpha_W(n):=\tfrac1n\#\{k:W(\alpha_{n,k})=1\},
\qquad
\mathrm{val}^\beta_W(n):=\tfrac1n\#\{k:W(\beta_{n,k})=1\}
\]
each taking the form $m/n$ for an integer $0\le m\le n$. Using these values, the addition of the threshold symbols to the language allows for the representation of a real-valued unknown rounded to the nearest $\frac{1}{n}$.

\paragraph{Contracts and quotes.}
Define the deferred contract $C_n$ and the quote ledger readout $R_n$ as affine combinations
\[
C_n:=\tfrac1n\sum_{k=1}^n\alpha_{n,k},
\qquad
R_n:=\tfrac1n\sum_{k=1}^n\beta_{n,k},
\]
so $W(C_n)=\mathrm{val}^\alpha_W(n)$ and $W(R_n)=\mathrm{val}^\beta_W(n)$
for consistent worlds $W$. Note that both $C_n$ and $R_n$ are affine combinations of symbols
already in the markets used for convenience rather than separately traded objects. Write
\[
a_n:=A_n(C_n)=\tfrac1n\sum_k A_n(\alpha_{n,k})\in\mathbb{Q}\cap[0,1]
\]
for $A$'s published quote on the deferred contract and
\[
Y_n:=H^+_{F(n)}(P^{(n)})
\]
for the eventual credence of $H^+$ that the contract uses for settlement. 

\paragraph{The more powerful reasoner.}
Let $\mathcal{C}_A\supseteq\mathcal{C}_H$ be a complexity class closed under
polynomial overhead for which the map $n\mapsto Y_n$ is $\mathcal{C}_A$-computable
in the coupled system. More precisely, given $n$, an implementation in $\mathcal{C}_A$ can simulate the mutual construction up to stage $F(n)$ and output $Y_n$. Writing $R(t)$ for the per-stage runtime of the
implementation of $H^+$, we assume $\mathcal{C}_A$ contains $n\mapsto R(F(n))$ (e.g.\ $\mathcal{C}_H=\mathrm{P}$, $\mathcal{C}_A=\mathrm{EXP}$, $F(n)=2^n$ when
$R$ is polynomial). This is a significant idealizing assumption about the computational power of $A$, but note that the fact that simulation is in the complexity class of $A$ doesn't entail that there is any efficient algorithm for traders to implement. Let $\sigma:\mathbb{N}^+\to\mathbb{N}^+$ be
$\mathcal{C}_A$-computable with $\sigma(n)>F(n)$ and such that $Y_n$ can be computed by this simulation
within $\sigma(n)$ steps.

\paragraph{The inductor $A$.}
We will now define $A$ and $H^+$ as two inductors that can see each other, constructed via recursion. For $0\le m\le n$ write the settling profile
\[
\mathcal{A}_n(m):=\{\alpha_{n,k}:k\le m\}\cup\{\neg\alpha_{n,k}:k>m\}
\]
and let
\[
m_n^*:=\argmin_{0\le m\le n}\left|\tfrac mn-Y_n\right|
\]
with ties going to the lower $m$. We therefore have
\[
\left|\tfrac{m_n^*}{n}-Y_n\right|\le\tfrac1{2n}
\]
because the grid $\{0,\frac1n,\frac2n,\ldots,1\}$ has mesh size $\frac1n$, so every value in $[0,1]$ is within $\frac1{2n}$ of some grid point. Define the computable deductive process
$D_A$ over $\mathcal{L}^\alpha$ as one that, for each time step $t$, $D_A^t$ includes:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
  \item the $\alpha$-monotonicity axioms for $n\le t$;
  \item for each $n$ with $\sigma(n)\le t$, the profile $\mathcal{A}_n(m_n^*)$.
\end{enumerate}
Each $D_A^t$ is finite (axiom schemata and settlement profiles are finite at any finite stage) and consistent (distinct $n$ touch disjoint symbols for both axioms and profiles, settlements are initial segments respecting monotonicity). $D_A$ is
computable as part of the mutual construction, since $\sigma(n)>F(n)$ makes $Y_n$ available from $H^+$
before its settlement is required by $D_A$. Let $A=(A_1,A_2,\ldots)$ be a universal
inductor over $D_A$ against $\mathcal{C}_A$.

\paragraph{The inductor $H^+$.}
Symmetrically write
\[
\mathcal{B}_n(\ell):=\{\beta_{n,k}:k\le\ell\}\cup\{\neg\beta_{n,k}:k>\ell\}
\]
and let
\[
\ell_n^*:=\argmin_{0\le\ell\le n}\left|\tfrac\ell n-a_n\right|
\]
with ties going to the lower $\ell$. This is the rounding of $A$'s posted quote. Define the computable deductive process $D_H^+$
over $\mathcal{L}^\beta$ as one that, for each time step $t$, $D_H^{+,t}$ includes:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
  \item $D_H^t$, so that $D_H^+$ extends the base human deductive process;
  \item the $\beta$-monotonicity axioms for $n\le t$;
  \item the profiles $\mathcal{B}_i(\ell_i^*)$ for each $i$ with $i < t$, i.e., the one-step-delayed record of $A$'s published quotes up to the prior time step.
\end{enumerate}
In other words, $D^+_H$ augments $D_H$ with feedback about the quotes produced by $A$. Each $D_H^{+,t}$ is finite and
consistent just as $D_A$ is, and it is computable as part of the
recursion since all of the values required for item 3 of the list above are available by time $t$. Let $H^+=(H^+_1,H^+_2,\ldots)$ be a universal inductor over $D_H^+$ against traders in $\mathcal{C}_H$.

\subsection*{Results}
\paragraph{Existence and well-foundedness.}
The four sequences $(A_t),(H^+_t),(D_A^t),(D_H^{+,t})$ are defined by one
recursion on $t$. $D_A^t$ depends on $H^+$ through values of $H^+_{F(i)}$ for $i$ with $\sigma(i)\le t$, hence $F(i)<\sigma(i)\le t$: prices
at times strictly below $t$. $D_H^{+,t}$ depends on $A$ only through quotes $a_i$
for $i<t$, again strictly below $t$. Neither market's stage-$t$ pricing
references the other's stage-$t$ pricing, so every stage-$t$ object is determined
by data from some stage less than $t$. Lemma 1 carries out the recursion and
verifies the two markets satisfy their logical induction criteria.

\begin{lemma}[Existence]\label{lem:existence} Assume the computational idealization in the construction: the map
\[
n\mapsto Y_n:=H^+_{F(n)}(P^{(n)})
\]
is $\mathcal{C}_A$-computable in the mutually defined system, and
$\sigma(n)>F(n)$ is a $\mathcal{C}_A$-computable schedule by which $Y_n$ can be
computed. Then the recursive construction of
\[
(A_t),\quad (H^+_t),\quad (D_A^t),\quad (D_H^{+,t})
\]
is well-founded. Moreover, each $D_A^t$ and $D_H^{+,t}$ is finite and
propositionally consistent, $A$ is a logical inductor over $D_A$ against
$\mathcal{C}_A$, and $H^+$ is a logical inductor over $D_H^+$ against
$\mathcal{C}_H$.
\end{lemma}
\paragraph{Limit calibration of $A$ tracking $H^+$.} Placeholder intro
\begin{theorem}[Tracking] In the coupled system above,\[
a_n-Y_n\to 0.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
A_n(C_n)-H^+_{F(n)}(P^{(n)})\to 0.
\] 
\end{theorem}
\paragraph{A reflection principle for $H^+$ about $A$.} We next turn to a form of reflection-style \footnote{In the sense of van Fraassen's reflection principle} trust created by this coupled system. The following theorem is a close variation of Garrabrant's Theorem 4.12.4 on Self-Trust in which $H^+$ conditions not on its own future credence directly, but on a quote from $A$ recorded in the $\beta$-ledger.

For a rational tolerance $\delta>0$ and a real-valued expression $X\in[0,1]$, define the one-sided continuous indicator
\[
\operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(X>p) :=
\begin{cases}
0 & X\le p,\\[2pt]
\dfrac{X-p}{\delta} & p<X<p+\delta,\\[4pt]
1 & X\ge p+\delta.
\end{cases}
\]
Define $\operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(X<p)$ analogously, i.e. with value 0 for $X$ at least $p$, value 1 for $X$ more than $\delta$ less than $p$, and linearly interpolated between 0 and 1 for $X$ at most $\delta$ less than $p$.

Recall that the quote readout (i.e. the price for the contract $C_n$ rounded to the $\frac{1}{n}$ grid) is defined as \[R_n:=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n\beta_{n,k}\]

We use the standard extension of logical induction from sentence-prices to expectations of bounded finite logically uncertain variables (LUVs).\footnote{Definition 4.8.1 of Garrabrant et al.} In particular, any bounded rational-valued function of finitely many sentences can be expanded as a finite affine combination of conjunctions over their truth profiles, priced by linearity. The variables appearing below, such as $1(P^{(n)})\cdot \operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(R_n>p_n)$, depend only on the finite family of atoms $\{\beta_{n,k}:1\le k\le n\}$ together with the sentence $P^{(n)}$, and so are legitimate bounded finite LUVs.

\begin{theorem}[External trust]\label{thm:external-trust}
Let $(p_n)$ be a $\mathcal{C}_H$-computable sequence of rational probabilities in
$[0,1]$, and let $\delta>0$ be rational. Write $1(P^{(n)})$ for the $[0,1]$-LUV representing the truth value of $P^{(n)}$. Then
\[
H^+_n\!\left(
1(P^{(n)})\cdot \operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(R_n>p_n)
\right)
\gtrsim_n
p_n\,
H^+_n\!\left(
\operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(R_n>p_n)
\right).
\]
Similarly,
\[
H^+_n\!\left(
1(P^{(n)})\cdot \operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(R_n<p_n)
\right)
\lesssim_n
p_n\,
H^+_n\!\left(
\operatorname{Ind}_{\delta}(R_n<p_n)
\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\paragraph{Underdetermination of the limit of $H$.} We now prove a theorem that 
characterizes a limitation of this setup. Despite the Tracking and External Trust results, use of $A$'s quotes does not guarantee $H^+$ is purely accelerated towards the original limit credences of $H$ for undecided sentences. In other words, augmenting $H^+$ with access to a computationally more powerful, trusted predictor of its own future credences is not a generally limit-conserving operation on inductors. Other conditions or machinery would be necessary to guarantee preservation of limiting credences.

For a computable nested finite sentence fragment $S_t$ containing $\phi$, let
$\Omega_t$ be the set of truth assignments on $S_t$ propositionally consistent
with $D^t$, let
\[
K_t:=\operatorname{conv}\{x(\omega):\omega\in\Omega_t\},
\]
and let
\[
K_t^c:=K_t\cap\{p:p(\phi)=c\}.
\]
Here $x(\omega)$ is the truth-value vector of $\omega$ on $S_t$, and the fragments
$S_t$ are taken to contain all sentences mentioned by the aggregate trader's
day-$t$ demand and current holdings, with $\bigcup_t S_t=\mathcal S$.

In the following lemma, $\mathcal T$ denotes the budgeted supertrader resulting from the `TradingFirm` construction in Garrabrant 5.3: an effective weighted sum of budgeted copies of all
traders in the relevant complexity class, with summable downside budgets. The construction guarantees that if
any trader in the class exploits the market, then $\mathcal T$ exploits the market.

\begin{lemma}[Constrained market-making]\label{lem:constrained-market-making}
Let $D$ be a consistent computable deductive process over a language
$\mathcal{L}$, and let $\phi$ be a sentence such that for every $t$,
\[
D^t\cup\{\phi\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
D^t\cup\{\neg\phi\}
\]
are both propositionally consistent. Fix a computable rational $c\in(0,1)$, and
let $K_t^c$ be as defined above. Let $\mathcal T$ be the budgeted supertrader described above. On day $t$, after the previous
price history has been fixed, each candidate current price vector
$p\in K_t^c$ determines a demand vector
\[
T_t(p)\in\mathbb R^{S_t},
\]
namely the vector of shares of the sentences in $S_t$ that $\mathcal T$ would buy
at current prices $p$. Suppose the market-maker chooses prices $p_t\in K_t^c$ such that, for some
computable summable error sequence $(\varepsilon_t)$,
\[
T_t(p_t)\cdot(q-p_t)\le \varepsilon_t
\]
for every alternative feasible price vector $q\in K_t^c$. Then $\mathcal T$ does not exploit the resulting market.
\end{lemma}


\begin{lemma}[Constrained inductors]\label{lem:constrained-li}
Let $D$ be a consistent computable deductive process over a language
$\mathcal{L}$, and let $\phi$ be a sentence such that for every $t$,
\[
D^t\cup\{\phi\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
D^t\cup\{\neg\phi\}
\]
are both propositionally consistent. Then for every computable rational
$c\in(0,1)$, there exists a computable logical inductor $P^c$ over $D$ such that
\[
\forall t,\ P^c_t(\phi)=c.
\]
\end{lemma}

construction of $A$ and $H^+$ as described above (in particular, one in which Theorems 1 and 2 hold) where
```

The polynomial-overhead closure requirement in Garrabrant's logical inductor framework ensures that when you combine multiple traders into a supertrader, the resulting system stays within the same complexity class. This is critical because the market-clearing mechanism (finding the fixed point each day) must be computable within the class's resource bounds, and the logical inductor algorithm itself runs in polynomial time when individual traders are polynomial-time — so closure under polynomial overhead guarantees the whole construction remains tractable.

In this paper, both $\mathcal{C}_H$ and $\mathcal{C}_A$ must be closed under polynomial overhead for their respective universal inductors $H$ and $H^+$ to exist, and since $\mathcal{C}_A \supseteq \mathcal{C}_H$, agent $A$ is strictly more powerful. The key question is how this complexity gap between the two classes actually determines the behavior and capabilities of the agents.

The gap becomes critical in the simulation assumption: $Y_n$ is computable by $A$ within its budget but not by $H$ within its own constraints, because $A$ can compute $H^+$'s future credence while $H^+$ cannot compute its own future credence faster than experiencing it in real time. Since the contract $C_n$ settles against $Y_n$, which lies in $\mathcal{C}_A$'s reach but outside $\mathcal{C}_H$'s grasp, this is where the complexity gap becomes essential—$A$ can price the contract with full information while $H$-class traders cannot shortcut to the answer.

The tracking mechanism depends entirely on this gap: $A$ can compute $Y_n$ quickly enough to provide calibrated, anticipatory quotes against it, making the advice genuinely informative. If both classes had equal computational power, $A$ couldn't compute $Y_n$ any faster than $H^+$ reaches it naturally, and the quotes would offer no real advantage—the gap is what makes $A$'s pricing actually predictive rather than redundant.

The gap itself doesn't affect the trust or non-conservativity bounds; those are determined by the logical-uncertainty interval and are independent of computational speed.
