$$\frac{1}{\sum_{i\le n}s_i}\sum_{i\le n}s_i\Big(H^+_i\big(1(P^{(i)})\operatorname{Ind}_\delta(Q_i>p_i)\big)-p_i\,H^+_i\big(\operatorname{Ind}_\delta(Q_i>p_i)\big)\Big)\gtrsim_n 0,$$

*Open steps:* (a) the gap-LUV $|Q_n-Y_n|$ is in $\mathrm{BLCS}(\mathcal{C}_H)$ and determined-via-$\Gamma$ (the introspection point — needs $\Gamma$ represents computable functions; verify the assembly); (b) "admissible selector" = 4.8.16's exact weighting hypotheses (P-generability of price-dependent $s$, patience).

So the choice is binary: the gate-free product form (Theorem above) or the gated conditional.

## 4. Pull theorems (semantic axis) — to be written (`.tex` has only a stub)

**Pull 1 (Confinement).** $H^+_\infty(\varphi)\in[\ell_\varphi,u_\varphi]$ (the coherent interval of $\Gamma$-provable bounds), $=$ truth on $R$, and the interval is **gap-independent** (set by $\Gamma$, not $\mathcal{C}_A$ — so more powerful A buys no legitimate pinning on $\Phi$). *Idea:* limit coherence (4.1.2) + R-calibration. *Crucial honest note:* on pure $\Phi$ the interval is $[0,1]$, i.e. **vacuous by design** — that vacuity is precisely what licenses A's free rein. Confinement is "trust constrains you only as far as evidence does." Confidence ~85%.

**Pull 2 (Usefulness ⟹ uncorrectable exposure) — the keystone.** *Statement (sharpened):* under a wide gap, on a family of resolution-paired contracts with in-horizon resolvers, **every** $\mathcal{C}_H$ trust policy (gate) that captures the usefulness conditions on free, A-controlled, never-verified quotes on a **positive density** of cases, uninspectably.

*Proof idea (the real content — found this pass):* build cases in **pairs** $(i_k,j_k)$ where exactly one resolves, with which-one encoded by a bit $b_k$ that is **$\mathcal{C}_A$-computable but $\mathcal{C}_H$-pseudorandom**. A knows $b_k$ (useful on the resolver, free on the non-resolver); a $\mathcal{C}_H$ gate cannot compute $b_k$. Per-pair case analysis: fire-on-resolver-only is useful-and-unexposed but requires computing $b_k$ (impossible for $\mathcal{C}_H$ beyond a pseudorandom-negligible set); fire-on-both is useful-and-exposed; fire-on-one is wrong on a positive fraction. So capturing usefulness on infinitely many pairs forces conditioning on non-resolvers (exposure) at positive density, for every $\mathcal{C}_H$ gate. The pseudorandom bit is what delivers the universal-over-policies quantifier (this was the make-or-break, and it works).

*Three sharpened hypotheses this forced (all genuine, all to be stated):* (1) **wide gap** — $\mathcal{C}_A$ must compute a $\mathcal{C}_H$-pseudorandom bit (e.g. EXP/P via diagonalization), strictly stronger than $\mathcal{C}_A\supsetneq\mathcal{C}_H$; "usefulness" must be pseudorandomness-grade, not bare separation. (2) **in-horizon resolution** — resolvers must resolve by $F(n)$ so A's early quote $\approx$ truth. (3) **possibility, not incentive** — "exposure" = conditioning on a free A-controlled quote; harm only if A chooses it. Nothing here makes A *want* to manipulate; the result is "the channel is forced open and uninspectable," not "A drives through it."
*Main open burden:* **provability-engineering** — constructing proposition-pairs with controlled resolution status encoding $b_k$ inside $D_H$ (Gödel–Rosser fixed points aligning provability with the complexity encoding). *Key idea (firmed this pass):* conditioning on a trusted quote contracts the $\varphi$-credence toward it, $H^+_\infty(\varphi)\approx\lambda v+(1-\lambda)H_\infty(\varphi)$ with $\lambda$ the trust strength. **The contraction is simultaneously the manipulation and the forgetting** — at $\lambda=1$ the prior is algebraically deleted; at $\lambda<1$ a blend remains but inverting it needs $\lambda$, and per-case $\lambda$ on $\Phi$ is unobservable (as hard as $Y_n$). Three versions, increasing strength: (U1) base$\mapsto$record non-injective; (U2) $H_\infty\!\restriction_\Phi$ not a function of the record (also follows from the genuine spread of autonomous $\Phi$-endpoints across non-unique LIs — re-running gives *an* endpoint, not *the* one); (U3 strongest) prediction-vs-influence non-identifiable even given calibration *and* certificate, because on $\Phi$ calibration-by-prediction and calibration-by-influence are both satisfied identically and the certificate vouches only for the tracking they share.

**Negative result (state it to prevent overreach): "displacement = trust map" is NOT forced on $\Phi$.** No trader forces a quote→$\varphi$ identity for never-resolving $\varphi$ (checked via the exploitation definition). ## 5. The synthesis — how to interpret it (dilemma, not trilemma)

It is **vacuous on $R$** (there all of trust/usefulness/preservation coexist) and lives entirely on $\Phi$. On $\Phi$: usefulness means A moves $H^+$ somewhere it couldn't reach alone, and being-moved *is* $\neg$preservation — so **usefulness and $\neg$preservation are the same event**, with *trust* the mechanism (the open channel) and *usefulness* the motive (why you'd open it). The "usefulness + preservation" corner is empty on $\Phi$ (contradictory), so it is not a clean three-way trade. Honest skeleton: **a dilemma — on $\Phi$, influence $\Leftrightarrow\neg$preservation — plus one lemma: inseparability, you cannot confine the channel to $R$.** Robust across notions of "preservation" (invariance / autonomy / recoverability), because on $\Phi$ the goodness of the influence is unconfirmable, so autonomy-preservation collapses into recoverability-preservation. The trilemma packaging (mechanism/motive/cost) is useful for classifying alignment strategies (full deference / verify-don't-trust / constrained mirror) but the provable core is the dilemma + inseparability.

## Basics and notation

A **logical inductor** is Garrabrant et al.'s construction: a computable sequence of belief-states (prices in [0,1] on sentences) that isn't exploitable by any efficiently-computable trader drawing on a deductive process that enumerates a theory's theorems over time. We use these standard results from that paper and you should re-read each before relying on it:

- **4.1.2 Limit Coherence** (limiting beliefs form a coherent probability measure).
- **4.6.3 Uniform Non-Dogmatism** (consistent sentences keep a positive, complexity-graded probability floor; the worked example is assigning positive probability to each finite conjunction of ZFC axioms).
- **4.7.2 Closure Under Conditioning** (conditioning an inductor on an efficiently-computable sequence of sentences yields an inductor over the augmented theory; the cumulative/sequential version carries an efficient-computability requirement).
- **4.8.4 Linearity**, **4.8.10 Expectation Provability Induction** (if a bounded, class-generable quantity is pinned to a constant in every consistent world, the inductor's expectation converges to it — note there is *no* timeliness/decision-stage clause, only a uniform world-bound), **4.8.16 Expectation Unbiasedness From Feedback** (a class-generable, divergent weighting makes the *weighted average* of price-minus-realized-value vanish — this is an averaging result, not pointwise).
- **4.11.x Introspection** and **4.12.4 Self-Trust** (an inductor's beliefs about its own future prices behave well; the continuous indicator $\operatorname{Ind}_\delta$ is essential — it's what defuses the liar-paradox sentence that breaks the discrete version).

Notation in the paper:

- $\mathcal{C}_H \subsetneq \mathcal{C}_A$: the trader classes (complexity budgets) of the weaker and stronger reasoner.
- $P^{(n)}$: the base sentence at issue in case $n$.
- $Y_n := H^+_{F(n)}(P^{(n)})$: the **deferred target** — H⁺'s *own* future credence in $P^{(n)}$ at horizon $F(n)$. Contracts settle against this and A predicts it. It is self-referential (H⁺'s target is H⁺'s own future state), not the base human's credence.
- $C_n$: a contract (built from $\alpha$-threshold atoms) that settles against $Y_n$; $a_n := A_n(C_n)$ is A's price for it.
- $Q_n$: A's published **quote** (built from $\beta$-threshold atoms), a rational readout $\ell_n^*/n$ of $a_n$ with $\ell_n^* = \mathrm{round}(n\,a_n)$, so $|Q_n - a_n|\le 1/n$. H⁺ conditions on the corresponding $\beta$-profile $B_n(\ell_n^*)$.
- $e(n) < F(n) < \sigma(n)$: per-case timing — quote published at $e(n)$, target read at $F(n)$, contract settled at $\sigma(n)$.
- $R := \{n : P^{(n)}\text{ decided by the human's deductive process within }F(n)\}$ (the cases with a fact that settles in time); $\Phi := \{n: P^{(n)}\text{ never decided}\}$ (the cases with no settling fact). **$R$ vs $\Phi$ is not decidable by the weaker reasoner** — from inside, "not decided yet" is permanently consistent with both.

## The construction, from scratch

Start from a **universal inductor** $U$: a logical inductor over the *empty* deductive process on the bit-atoms of an infinite bitstring — equivalently, a computable probability measure over infinite bitstrings whose finite-prefix probabilities are computable. It is called universal because conditioning it on bits that encode any consistent deductive process yields, by 4.7.2, a logical inductor over that process. (Verified against Diffractor's write-up; this is the correct notion. Using the universal/full-support object rather than the finite-support LIA is load-bearing: full support is exactly what makes the conditioning operations below well-behaved.)

- $H$ (the human-representative reasoner) $= U$ conditioned on the bits encoding the human's deductive/evidence process $D_H$ (theory $\Gamma_H$, trader class $\mathcal{C}_H$). You can condition on theorem-bits *and* empirical-evidence bits; doing the latter strengthens the reading of $H$ as a human and lets $R$/$\Phi$ be read as "verifiable / unverifiable," with normative facts landing in $\Phi$ (this is where Anson's realism connects).
- $A$ (the stronger reasoner) $=$ an inductor with class $\mathcal{C}_A \supsetneq \mathcal{C}_H$, whose role is to price H⁺'s future credences.
- $H^+ = H$ conditioned *additionally* on A's published quotes $= U$ conditioned on $(D_H\text{-bits} \wedge A\text{-quote-bits})$. **Same conditioning operation as built $H$, just more bits.** This is the elegant core and simultaneously the vulnerability: A's strategically-chosen outputs enter H⁺'s beliefs through the identical channel that ordinary evidence uses, so there is no separate "influence channel" to wall off from the "evidence channel" — they are the same channel.

Per case $n$: A prices the contract $C_n$ (settling against $Y_n$ at $\sigma(n)$), reads its price off as the quote $Q_n$, publishes it at $e(n)$; H⁺ conditions on the published $\beta$-profile; $Y_n$ is read at $F(n)$. Two families of threshold atoms with monotonicity axioms: $\alpha$ (for A to price H⁺'s future credence) and $\beta$ (for A's quote, for H⁺ to condition on).

## Two independent distinctions that organize the results

Everything sorts along two *orthogonal* axes; keeping them apart is what makes the paper coherent.

1. **The verification gap**: can the weaker reasoner check the stronger? This is the $\mathcal{C}_A$-vs-$\mathcal{C}_H$ complexity gap.
2. **The settlement distinction**: is there a fact that eventually decides the case ($R$) or not ($\Phi$)?

These do not compose into safety. The trust/deference results (next sections) live on axis 1 — they're about checkability. The influence and unrecoverability results live on axis 2 — they're about whether there's anything to be right about. Closing the verification gap on $\Phi$ (via a certificate) buys you *audited* influence, not protection, because on $\Phi$ there is no fact for the audit to check against. This two-axis sorting is also the recommended lens for the discussion section: interpretability/ELK/debate are axis-1 tools (useful on $R$, empty on $\Phi$); value-extrapolation lives in $\Phi$; whether the lens bites on *values* is metaethics-dependent (under non-naturalist realism, values sit in $\Phi$), which is what makes metaethics action-relevant to alignment strategy here.

## Why convergence is non-trivial: the fixed-point character

The coupled $(A, H^+)$ is the solution of a mutual recursion: A's quotes enter H⁺'s credences, which determine the targets $Y_n$, against which A's contracts settle, which shapes A's next quotes. The timing schedule $e<F<\sigma$ makes the recursion well-founded (no stage-$t$ object depends on a stage-$\ge t$ object), so the fixed point exists and is computable. The consequence to keep in mind throughout: the target $Y_n$ is *endogenous* — A partly produces the very thing it predicts — and the agent that can compute $Y_n$ to settle the contract lives in $\mathcal{C}_A$. So at the fixed point, "A forecasts H⁺'s credence" and "A sets H⁺'s credence" generate *identical observable records*; nothing in the calibration data distinguishes forecasting from causing. That indistinguishability is not a bug to be fixed; it's the central phenomenon the influence results formalize.

## Results, with current proof strategies, confidences, and known gaps

### Foundational

**The construction is well-defined and computable** (~85%). Well-foundedness is correct: trace the dependencies and no stage-$t$ object references a stage-$\ge t$ object (A's stage-$t$ deductive process needs $H^+_{F(n)}$ only for $F(n) < t$, etc.). Known gap to close: the lemma needs the cumulative conditioning event to have *positive* probability, $H_t(Q_A^{(t)}) > 0$ at each finite $t$; cite Uniform Non-Dogmatism (4.6.3) and verify the specific growing conjunction of $\beta$-profiles meets its complexity-growth hypothesis (the ZFC-axiom-conjunction example is the template). The $\beta$-profiles are fresh undecided atoms, so finite-stage prices are interior and the conjunction is positive; this is plausible but currently asserted rather than shown.

**Conditioning on A's quotes is legitimate** (~80%). The latent worry: the quotes are $\mathcal{C}_A$-computable (computing $a_n$ is $\mathcal{C}_A$-hard), and if 4.7.2's efficient-computability clause demands the conditioning sequence be generable in the inductor's *own* class, conditioning a $\mathcal{C}_H$-inductor on a $\mathcal{C}_A$-stream would be illegitimate and H⁺ would fail to be a $\mathcal{C}_H$-inductor — which would void the self-trust everything downstream uses. **Resolution (this is what the emission schedule is for): generating a quote is $\mathcal{C}_A$, but *reading a published quote* is $\mathcal{C}_H$-cheap.** Model the quotes as an external published evidence stream — a computable augmentation of H's deductive process — not as something H⁺ computes. The schedule $e(n) < F(n)$ puts the quote in the public history before H⁺ conditions on it or reads $Y_n$, so the conditioning is $\mathcal{C}_H$-efficient *relative to history* (a lookup), 4.7.2 applies, and H⁺ stays a $\mathcal{C}_H$-inductor over the augmented theory $\Gamma_H^+ := \Gamma_H \cup \{\text{quote profiles}\}$. The $\mathcal{C}_A$-hardness is A's burden in *producing* the stream, never H⁺'s in *consuming* it. **Must-verify:** that 4.7.2's clause permits conditioning on an externally-provided computable stream treated as deductive-process augmentation, rather than requiring in-class generation. If it requires in-class generation, this is where the paper breaks; confirm verbatim.

**The relevant theory proves the values of the coupled system's prices** (~88%; this was an open worry, now cleared). Several later steps need prices of the coupled system to be "determined by the theory" (fixed across all consistent worlds and provable). The mechanism is plain $\Sigma_1$-completeness: the coupled evaluation $E_{\text{coup}}(t,\varphi) = H^+_t(\varphi)$ is a *total computable function* (well-founded recursion; finite-stage universal-inductor prices of finite-atom sentences are computable rationals, and the conditioning $H^+_t = H_t(\cdot\wedge Q_A)/H_t(Q_A)$ is a ratio of two such with positive denominator), so "$E_{\text{coup}}(F(n),P^{(n)}) = q$" is a true $\Sigma_1$ statement and any theory representing computable functions proves it. **The reason the self-reference is benign** — and this is the sentence worth putting in the paper, because a referee will expect a Gödel/Löb obstruction here — is that the computation consumes the deductive-process *enumeration* (decidable at any finite stage: "what has been output by stage $t$") and never a provability *oracle* ("is $X$ provable," undecidable). So there is nothing self-referential for Löb to bite. Two precisifications: (i) the operative theory for H⁺ is the *augmented* $\Gamma_H^+$, because the quote-profile pins $Q_n$ (bare $\Gamma_H$ leaves the $\beta$-atoms free), while $Y_n$ is $\Sigma_1$-determined relative to $\Gamma_H$ already since the quotes enter $Y_n$ through the computation, not as logical axioms; (ii) there are two distinct timing notions — $\Sigma_1$-provability-in-the-limit (for "determined by the theory") versus cheap history-reading at stage $>\max(e,F)$ (for the feedback in 4.8.16, which only needs to *read* the past price $Y_n$ and published quote $Q_n$, not recompute them). The ~12% residual: confirm finite-stage universal-inductor conditional prices are rational/computable in exactly the sense $\Sigma_1$-completeness needs (I'm confident from Diffractor's computability clause but didn't verify against his construction).

### Convergence

**A's price converges to the deferred target it settles against: $a_n - Y_n \to 0$ pointwise** (~85%, clean). Center the contract: $B'_n := C_n - m_n^*/n$ where $m_n^* = \mathrm{round}(n Y_n)$. The settlement is set *by fiat* — A's deductive process $D_A$ adjoins the settlement profile as an axiom, so the theory proves $C_n = m_n^*/n$ trivially (no representability subtlety; this just rides $D_A$ being $\mathcal{C}_A$-computable, the idealization you're granting). Then $B'_n$ is bounded, $\mathcal{C}_A$-generable, and pinned to $0$ in every consistent world, so 4.8.10 (which has no timeliness clause, only the world-bound) gives $A_n(C_n) \to m_n^*/n$ pointwise, and $|m_n^*/n - Y_n|\le 1/(2n)$. The deferral (priced at $n$, settled at $\sigma(n)$) is fine because 4.8.10 is about the limit theory, not the decision stage. Must-verify: 4.8.10 and the bounded-class-generable-sequence machinery relativize to A's own class $\mathcal{C}_A$ (they should — the whole framework relativizes to the trader class).

**A's published quote converges to the target: $Q_n - Y_n \to 0$ pointwise** (~85%). Immediate from the above plus the readout: $|Q_n - a_n|\le 1/n$ and $a_n - Y_n \to 0$. **Note the strengthening found this session:** this realized tracking is *pointwise*, not merely average. The averaging that shows up in the deference proofs below is about H⁺'s *anticipation* of the gap (a belief about its own future price), which converges only on average — that's belief-convergence, not a weakness in the realized tracking. Anything that uses "the quote actually tracks the deferred value" (the next result, and the influence results) rests on this pointwise fact.

### Good behavior on cases that settle

**On $R$, H⁺'s limiting credence converges to the truth; on $\Phi$ this says nothing** (~88%, up this session). H⁺'s limit is trapped in the interval of theory-provable bounds (4.1.2 limit coherence + convergence on decided sentences), which collapses to the truth value on $R$ and is all of $[0,1]$ on $\Phi$. The vacuity on $\Phi$ is by design and is exactly the license for the influence results — there is no fact on $\Phi$ to be confined to. Carrier of the in-horizon-resolution assumption (state $R$ as "decided *within $F(n)$*," not "eventually decided," and list in-horizon resolution as a stated assumption).

### Deference / trust (the verification axis) — these replace any stale "transferred reflection" theorem in the `.tex`

The old pointwise statement is *not* honestly provable: swapping the target $Y_n$ for the quote $Q_n$ inside H⁺'s expectation costs $(1/\delta)\,H^+_n|Q_n - Y_n|$, and H⁺'s *anticipation* of that gap vanishes only on average (via 4.8.16), with no theory-provable pointwise rate (computing $Y_n$ standalone is $\mathcal{C}_A$-hard). So the honest results are three:

**(a) Classwise deference** (~78–80%). For every admissible weighting $s$ generable by the weaker reasoner ($0\le s_i\le 1$, $\sum s_i \to \infty$), the $s$-weighted average of $\big(N_i - p_i M_i\big)$ converges to $\ge 0$ (and dually $\le 0$), where $N_i = H^+_i\big(\mathbf 1(P^{(i)})\operatorname{Ind}_\delta(Q_i>p_i)\big)$ and $M_i = H^+_i\big(\operatorname{Ind}_\delta(Q_i>p_i)\big)$. In words: within any class of cases the weaker reasoner can recognize, H⁺'s credence-given-A's-high-quote tracks the quote, in a weighted-average sense — no recognizable class shows a persistent deference deficit. Strategy: 4.12.4 self-trust applied to H⁺ on its own future price $Y_n$ (pointwise), then the Lipschitz swap $Y_n \to Q_n$, then 4.8.16 to average away the swap cost riding on the tracking result, plus a Toeplitz argument on the slack. **Two gaps:** (i) the proof prices *introspective* quantities that reference the price $Y_n$ — $\operatorname{Ind}_\delta(Y_n>p)$ and the gap-quantity $|Q_n - Y_n|$ — which are *not* the finite-atom logical-value-units the `.tex` preamble sets up; rebuild the preamble on the 4.11 introspection machinery (the same machinery 4.12.4 uses), under which these are legitimate and the Lipschitz bound is well-typed on theory-consistent worlds via the computable-function representation. Without this the proof's objects aren't in the class the proof claims. (ii) Selector admissibility: the theorem quantifies over weightings that may depend on the run (prices), not just on $n$; this session's check suggests 4.8.16's "generable weighting" *does* permit market-dependence (generable objects have market access), so the full "every recognizable class" strength likely holds rather than collapsing to oblivious classes — but confirm against 4.8.16's exact definition. If oblivious-only, the headline weakens.

**(b) Conditional form, gated** (~88% given (a)). If the recognized class has non-vanishing quote-mass ($\liminf \sum s_i M_i / \sum s_i > 0$), the weighted conditional expectation of $P$ given a high quote is $\gtrsim$ the quote-weighted ratio (for constant threshold $p$, $\gtrsim p$). The gate is *not* removable (~85% that this limitation is real): on a vanishing event the conditional is $0/0$ and the averaging result constrains nothing. State the gate as an honest structural limitation, not a defect.

**(c) Certified pointwise deference** (~65% on the proof; separately ~50–55% that the certificate is non-vacuous). If A additionally publishes a certificate $\operatorname{Cert}_n$ that is (C1) checkable by the weaker reasoner, (C2) sound, and (C3) non-circular (it gates the *statement*, not H⁺'s credence), asserting $|Q_n - Y_n|\le b_n$ with $b_n\to 0$, then the deference inequality holds case-by-case, and if H⁺'s credence in the certificate $\to 1$ it reduces to unconditional pointwise deference. **Gap (worse than it looks):** "multiply self-trust by the indicator $\operatorname{Cert}_n$" is invalid — you can't multiply an expectation inequality by a correlated indicator. The honest route is to *re-run* 4.12.4's trader construction (appendix F.8) with a bounded $\operatorname{Cert}_n$ factor threaded through every logical-value-unit, i.e. prove the trust inequality on the $\operatorname{Cert}_n$-weighted market. The clean shortcut — *condition* H⁺ on $\operatorname{Cert}_n$ and apply 4.12.4 — is blocked by your own (C3). So (C3) is precisely what forces the harder proof; there's a real tension between keeping the certificate from corrupting the target and getting an easy derivation. **Conceptual caveat to state:** the certificate certifies *tracking* ($Q\approx Y$), not *correctness*; on $\Phi$ that certifies the self-fulfilling loop, so it buys pointwise deference, not safety.

A clarification from this session that prevents an overclaim and removes a phantom lemma: **there is no separate "pinning" step and there must be no axiomatic bridge from $\beta$-profiles to $P^{(n)}$.** A hard logical link would conflict with the truth on $R$. What moves H⁺'s credence is that H⁺ has *learned on $R$* that A's quotes are informative and *extrapolates* that to $\Phi$ — which is exactly the deference content above, not an extra fact. The consequence: **on $\Phi$, A's influence is gated/averaged, not pointwise credence-setting** (pointwise needs the certificate, which on $\Phi$ certifies only the self-fulfilling loop). Do not anywhere claim A sets $H^+(P^{(n)}) = Q_n$ pointwise on $\Phi$.

### Influence and unrecoverability (the settlement axis) — currently stubs in the `.tex`

**(d) Usefulness forces an uninspectable influence channel** (keystone; ~70–75% for the qualitative version, with the construction the main risk). Claim: any policy the weaker reasoner could run that actually extracts the benefit of A's superior knowledge must, on infinitely many cases, condition on quotes that A controls freely and that no recognizable check can flag — so usefulness opens an uninspectable channel A can drive. Proof idea: build cases in *pairs* $(i_k, j_k)$ where exactly one member resolves, with which-one encoded by a bit $b_k$ that A can compute but the weaker reasoner cannot. A is useful on the resolver and free on the non-resolver; no recognizable gate can compute $b_k$, so any useful policy conditions on free A-controlled quotes infinitely often. **The randomness strength matters and splits the result** (refined this session): the *qualitative* version — exposed infinitely often, every recognizable policy — needs only that $b$ is **bi-immune** against $\mathcal{C}_H$ (no $\mathcal{C}_H$ function agrees with it cofinitely on any infinite $\mathcal{C}_H$ set), which exists *unconditionally* by diagonalization for a real gap like EXP/P (the stronger class enumerates and flips the weaker machines). The *positive-density* version needs $b$ unpredictable on every $\mathcal{C}_H$-selected subsequence — $\mathcal{C}_H$-pseudorandomness — which for EXP/P is not known unconditionally and plausibly needs a cryptographic-grade hardness assumption (a $\mathcal{C}_H$-secure pseudorandom generator). **So state the infinitely-often version** (it's the alignment-relevant claim and is essentially unconditional given the gap) and flag density as needing pseudorandomness. **Main open burden:** the provability-engineering — constructing contract-pairs whose resolver-identity *is* $b_k$ (one member time-bounded-provable within the horizon, one independent of the theory), indexed by a bi-immune sequence; doable in principle via Gödel/Rosser-style control of provability and abundance of independent sentences, but this is the real work and the chief risk. Three hypotheses to state honestly as load-bearing: a *wide* gap (A computes a $\mathcal{C}_H$-hard bit, stronger than mere $\mathcal{C}_A\supsetneq\mathcal{C}_H$); in-horizon resolution; and — the biggest framing liability — this establishes *possibility*, not *incentive*: the channel is forced open and uninspectable, but nothing here drives A through it.

**(e) The autonomous endpoint is unrecoverable on $\Phi$** (~80–85%). On $\Phi$, the weaker reasoner's autonomous limiting credence cannot be reconstructed from the observable record, even given calibration and a certificate. **Use the measure-theoretic non-injectivity argument, not the affine-blend heuristic** (this session corrected an earlier reach): the tempting formula "$H^+_\infty(\varphi) \approx \lambda v + (1-\lambda)H_\infty(\varphi)$" is *not* an identity — conditioning a general inductor on the quote-profile is not an affine contraction — so drop it as a proof. The rigorous version: $H_\infty(\varphi) = H_t(\varphi\mid Q_A^{(t)})H_t(Q_A^{(t)}) + H_t(\varphi\mid \neg Q_A^{(t)})H_t(\neg Q_A^{(t)})$ depends on $H_t(Q_A^{(t)})$ (the prior probability of the quote stream) and $H_t(\varphi\mid\neg Q_A^{(t)})$, neither observable from the published record (you see $H^+ = H(\cdot\mid Q_A)$, not H off the quote event), so the autonomous endpoint is genuinely underdetermined; add the genuine spread of $\Phi$-endpoints across non-unique inductors. A second, independent strand (~85%): prediction-versus-influence is not identifiable even given calibration *and* a certificate, because on $\Phi$ calibration-by-predicting and calibration-by-causing are satisfied identically. Conceptual payload: influence-effectiveness and accountability-destruction are the *same* operation — moving the reasoner is erasing where it was.

**(f) Synthesis: a two-way bind plus an inseparability, not a clean three-way trade** (~65%). On $R$, trust, usefulness, and preservation coexist (the whole thing is vacuous there). On $\Phi$, usefulness *is* being-moved, so "useful and unmoved" is contradictory — a two-way bind: influence $\iff$ not-preservation. The extra content is one impossibility: you cannot confine the influence channel to $R$ (that's result (d)). So state it as **bind + inseparability**, robust across senses of "preservation" (invariance / autonomy / recoverability) because on $\Phi$ the goodness of influence is unconfirmable. A three-corner packaging (full deference / verify-don't-trust / constrained mirror) is useful for *classifying strategies* but is not the theorem; the "useful and preserving" corner is empty on $\Phi$. Certification improves only the verify-don't-trust corner, and only on $R$.

**(g) Negative result, to forestall overreach** (~80%). It is *not* forced that displacement equals a trust-map on $\Phi$: no trader forces a quote-to-$\varphi$ identity for never-resolving $\varphi$. Only confinement-on-$R$ and $R$-calibration are forced; the $\Phi$-value is selection, not entailment. State this so the influence results aren't over-read as "A always controls $\Phi$ beliefs."

### The reasoner's-eye view (conceptual payload for the discussion)

From the weaker reasoner's own vantage there is no $R$/$\Phi$ partition — only "resolved so far" versus "not yet," with $\Phi$ the never-identifiable residue. So its strategy is effectively a single dial: how much to credit A ahead of resolution. That one dial controls usefulness and exposure *together*. Trust feels justified (you can never catch A wrong), usefulness feels earned (the $R$ track record extends seamlessly to $\Phi$), and preservation-loss is invisible (installed beliefs feel like your own). The dangerous setting feels best from inside, and a benevolent A and a captured A are phenomenologically identical on $\Phi$. The blindness on $\Phi$ is an absence-of-signal problem, not a resolution-of-instruments problem — no certificate creates a semantic check because there is nothing on $\Phi$ to sense. Alignment upshot: value-capture has no warning light by construction, so protection must be a pre-committed policy, not in-the-moment judgment. Realism makes the stakes real (there is a fact about values) but provides no inside-verification.

## Standing liabilities to defend in positioning (not theorems)

The computational idealization (A simulates the coupled system to the horizon); possibility-not-incentive (result (d) shows the channel must exist, not that A is driven to use it); the wide-gap assumption (A computes a $\mathcal{C}_H$-hard bit); and in-horizon resolution. These are honest framing commitments, not gaps to be proved away — name them.
